title: Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 â the best pictures so far
author: Maddie Molloy
content:
![A polar bear peers down through a roughly circular opening in the white ice, its entire face visible through the hole. Its dark nose and eyes stand out against its pale fur, while the vivid blue sky beyond the opening contrasts with the darker edge of the ice.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/db40/live/d4ab0780-9baa-11f1-92e6-b1dfcecd4308.jpg)
This image titled Icy Window was highly commended in the "Animal Portraits" category
- Published
How would it feel to find yourself face to face with one of the Arctic's most formidable predators?
This stunning image captures life from a seal's perspective. Taken by Norwegian wildlife photographer Audun Rikardsen, it was among the 'Highly Commended' entries in this year's Wildlife Photographer of the Year competition.
While working as a guide with Arctic Wildlife Tours, Rikardsen rigged an underwater camera with a motion sensor beneath a seal's breathing hole, and then waited. At 4am, a female polar bear approached and peered down.
Rikardsen then waited eight hours for the bear to move away before retrieving the camera and reviewing the images.
When he saw what he had captured, he said: "I was so extremely happy. I was screaming, so I probably woke up all the polar bears for miles."
Rikardsen has previously won two Wildlife Photographer of the Year categories: Birds in 2019 and Oceans: The Bigger Picture in 2025.
The overall winners will be announced on Tuesday 13 October 2026, followed by an exhibition at the Natural History Museum in London, external from Friday 16 October 2026.
Scroll down to explore other highly commended works from the competition.
![A brown swift glides beneath a passenger airplane, their similar wing shapes echoing each other against the blue sky.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/4cae/live/4318c250-8f14-11f1-b2ab-0dd01740f9f6.jpg)
Title: The Art of Flying
Photographer: Jack Crockford (UK)
Category: Highly Commended, 15-17 Years
Location: Bushy Park, London
Crockford watched swifts return to London after their annual migration from Africa, filling the air with their high-pitched calls. Most flew too high to photograph, but a few lower-flying ones gave Crockford the opportunity to capture the picture he wanted.
Swifts spend almost their entire lives in the air, usually landing only to nest.
![A small Eastern Japanese toad sits on a wet metal storm drain in the middle of a city street at night. Its body is sharply focused in the foreground, while a silhouetted person walks away in the background. Colourful street and building lights glow as soft reflections across the wet pavement.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1536/cpsprodpb/c605/live/3fcbba30-8f14-11f1-a7ab-8b30adf0800a.jpg)
Title: Urban Wanderer
Photographer: Sora Miyazawa (Japan)
Category: Highly Commended, 11-14 Years
Location: Tokyo, Japan
After rainfall, Miyazawa came across an Eastern Japanese toad making its way along a city street. He used a slow shutter speed to photograph it before it hopped back into the bushes.
Eastern Japanese toads are typically found in forests, grasslands and other terrestrial habitats across eastern Japan, but they have also proved remarkably adaptable to urban environments.
![Two adult orcas swim just below the surface of deep blue water, viewed from above, with one carrying the body of a deceased calf on the tip of its nose. At the upper right of the frame, the tips of two more orcasâ tails can be seen as they swim deeper into the water. There are ripples in the surrounding water.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/b08c/live/3bd049a0-8f14-11f1-b2ab-0dd01740f9f6.jpg)
Title: Lifted to the Surface
Photographer: Vegard Byrkjeland Aasen (Norway)
Category: Highly Commended, Behaviour: Mammals
Location: KvÃ¦nangen, Troms County, Norway
Aasen was flying a drone for the Norwegian Orca Survey when he noticed an adult orca carrying the body of a deceased calf through a Norwegian fjord.
The orca repeatedly allowed the calf to sink before bringing it back to the surface, a difficult moment to watch but one that Aasen felt was important to record.
The behaviour may have been an attempt to revive or protect the calf. Killer whales have previously been observed carrying deceased calves, including a case where a female Southern Resident killer whale carried her dead calf for at least 17 days.
A 2026 study, external suggests that this type of behaviour may be more widespread across the species than previously thought.
![A close-up photograph of a fer-de-lance viper facing directly towards the camera. Its broad head, pale tan facial markings and textured scales are clearly visible, with a small mosquito perched on top of its head. The snakeâs patterned body fills the lower part of the image, while the earthy background is softly out of focus.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/7ced/live/f714c7b0-8f17-11f1-a7ab-8b30adf0800a.jpg)
Title: Biting Back
Photographer: Andrea & Maceo Grammatico (France)
Category: Highly Commended, Animal Portraits
Location: Sierpe, South Puntarenas, Costa Rica
Only when they reviewed the images did the Grammatico twins realise they had captured a mosquito resting on the head of a fer-de-lance viper. They described it as "one of the most demanding focus stacks we've ever created".
Highly venomous and responsible for more fatal snake bites in Central America than any other species, the fer-de-lance is well camouflaged and can blend into plantation habitats, sometimes going unnoticed by workers.
![A black vulture stands in shallow water with both wings fully spread over the carcass of a yacarÃ© caiman. Parts of the caimanâs body emerge from the surrounding darkness, with the almost black background.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/701b/live/4f6c6de0-8f14-11f1-b2ab-0dd01740f9f6.jpg)
Title: Wings of Darkness
Photographer: Andy Parkinson (UK)
Category: Highly Commended, Animal Portraits
Location: Meeting of the Waters State Park, Northern Pantanal, Brazil
Parkinson photographed a black vulture perched over a dead yacarÃ© caiman in Brazil's Pantanal wetlands, keeping his boat at a distance and using a long telephoto lens to capture the shot.
A jaguar waiting out of frame emerged after the vulture flew away to claim the carcass. Only then did Parkinson notice a suspiciously clean, straight wound on the back of the caiman's head, possibly caused by a blow from a speeding boat, he suspects.
![A Namaqua chameleon emerges from a cloud of blowing sand, with its head and upper body rising above the rippled desert surface. Its rough, textured skin and a row of small raised scales along its back are clearly visible, while swirling sand creates a hazy, monochromatic desert scene.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1680/cpsprodpb/7208/live/5424ece0-8f14-11f1-b8ee-9b3c26ad07bb.jpg)
Title: Eye of the Storm
Photographer: Dewald Tromp (South Africa)
Category: Highly Commended, Animals in their Environment
Location: Namib Desert, near Swakopmund, Namibia
Tromp was photographing a Namaqua chameleon in the Namib Desert when the wind suddenly intensified, bringing a sandstorm that quickly reduced visibility and made breathing difficult.
These chameleons are desert specialists and can obtain moisture directly from the air. Dew gathers on their skin and is channelled towards their mouths through microscopic grooves, while their tongues can also collect fog water condensed on plants, sand and rocks.
![A vast flock of birds fills the air, their dark silhouettes swirling against a warm, golden-brown sky. Through the hazy atmosphere near the bottom of the image, the silhouettes of deer-shaped animals can be seen.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/61ce/live/59291ae0-8f14-11f1-a7ab-8b30adf0800a.jpg)
Title: Flock of Gold
Photographer: Bence MÃ¡tÃ© (Hungary) - 2010 Wildlife Photographer winner
Category: Highly Commended, Behaviour: Birds
Location: Ashnil Aruba Lodge, Tsavo East National Park, Kenya
MÃ¡tÃ© was watching birds gather at a small pond when tens of thousands of red-billed queleas swept down to drink in the golden late-afternoon light. The movement of so many wings created a rush of air that, he says, could be felt from 30m (98ft) away.
Red-billed queleas can gather in flocks of up to two million and are considered the most abundant wild bird on Earth, with an estimated 1.5 billion breeding adults.
![A close-up of a rhinocerosâs head, showing its wrinkled grey skin, eye and large horn. A small dark red-billed oxpecker with a vivid red-orange beak perches on the rhinoâs head near the base of its horn. The background is softly blurred, with warm sandy-brown tones.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/1795/live/64cd73a0-8f14-11f1-b2ab-0dd01740f9f6.jpg)
Title: Mutual Friends
Photographer: Ernest Porter (South Africa)
Category: Highly Commended, Behaviour: Birds
Location: Manyeleti Game Reserve, Mpumalanga, South Africa
While searching the reserve for wildlife, Porter photographed a red-billed oxpecker rubbing its bill against a white rhino's skin in the afternoon light. The birds feed on insects living on rhinos and can also act as sentinels - calling to warn their hosts when danger approaches. In Swahili, the red-billed oxpecker is known as askari wa kifaru, meaning "the rhino's guard".
![A black-and-white photograph shows a tall, vertically ridged tree trunk against a bright white background. The front paws of a young leopard can be seen clinging to the trunk, along with a small portion of the top of its head. The rest of its body is obscured by the trunk. Near the top of the trunk, a squirrel is visible in full, facing downwards.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1376/cpsprodpb/7c58/live/6ac79a60-8f14-11f1-b8ee-9b3c26ad07bb.jpg)
Title: Up a Tree without a Squirrel
Photographer: Allegra Hutton (USA)
Category: Highly Commended, Behaviour: Mammals
Location: Okavango Delta, Botswana
Hutton had watched a young leopard pursue a squirrel into a tree, having earlier seen the cat unsuccessfully attempt to stalk a rabbit. The squirrel escaped by climbing higher, leaving the leopard clinging on before it eventually made an awkward retreat.
For young leopards, survival is far from guaranteed: fewer than half reach independence, with male leopards, lions and other predators among the threats they face.
![A mottled green and brown bullfrog crouches low on muddy ground with its mouth open and its long pink tongue extended toward a small butterfly flying just above it. The frogâs textured skin and bright eye are sharply in focus against a softly blurred, earthy background.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/399b/live/70e6d550-8f14-11f1-a7ab-8b30adf0800a.jpg)
Title: Split-Second Escape
Photographer: Jens Cullmann (Germany)
Category: Highly Commended, Behaviour: Amphibians and Reptiles
Location: Central Kalahari Game Reserve, Botswana
An African bullfrog lunges for a babul butterfly but misses.
Cullmann had noticed tadpoles on a previous visit after heavy rains and returned the following month to find ponds and puddles full of young bullfrogs. He spent more than two weeks watching the young frogs "eat everything that moved".
As adults, African bullfrogs can reach 12cm (4.7in) in length and spend around 10 months of the year dormant underground, emerging after the rains to breed and feed voraciously.
![A pale green lichen dragon katydid is almost completely camouflaged among delicate, branching pale green foliage. Its long, slender body and legs blend closely with the thin stems but the dark background makes the insect stand out.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/db20/live/758849e0-8f14-11f1-a7ab-8b30adf0800a.jpg)
Title: Hidden Dragon
Photographer: Gil Wizen (Israel/Canada)
Category: Highly Commended, Behaviour: Invertebrates
Location: Wildsumaco Biological Station, Napo Province, Ecuador
Wizen was photographing a lichen dragon katydid measuring just 15mm long, making it difficult to distinguish from the lichen around it. He spotted the insect when it moved, but even then struggled to separate it from its background through the viewfinder.
Found only in Ecuador's Andes Mountains, its spiny armour helps protect it from eagle-eyed predators that can see through its disguise.
![A dramatic split-level ocean photograph shows lots of fish schooling in dark blue water beneath a shoreline silhouetted against glowing orange clouds, with a faint rainbow in the distance.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/8ebf/live/7bfb4a20-8f14-11f1-a7ab-8b30adf0800a.jpg)
Title: Calm Amid the Storm
Photographer: Shane Gross (Canada) - 2024 Wildlife Photographer winner
Category: Highly Commended, Oceans: The Bigger Picture
Location: D'Arros Island, Seychelles
Gross was photographing a school of bigeye trevally near the shore at sunrise as a storm approached. To create a split-level image, he turned his camera upside down to aid buoyancy distribution and slowly moved towards the curious fish.
Bigeye trevally are fished in many parts of the world, but here they are relatively safe. In 2023, the waters surrounding D'Arros Island were made a Marine Protected Area and designated as a no-take zone as part of the worldwide initiative for governments to protect 30% of Earth's land and ocean by 2030.
![A brown bear sits in the shallow end of a swimming pool, leaning against the tiled edge with one of its back paws raised, appearing to scratch it's face. White balls and a pink doughnut-shaped inflatable ring float nearby. The pool is surrounded by a paved patio, artificial grass, white lounge chairs, and a red sign saying California hanging on the white bricked fence.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/7926/live/87e70c20-8f14-11f1-b8ee-9b3c26ad07bb.jpg)
Title: Pooltime Pastime
Photographer: Loren Elliott (USA)
Category: Highly Commended, Urban Wildlife
Location: Monrovia, California, USA
Elliott spent hours watching through the kitchen window of a local resident's home, hoping to photograph black bears that frequently pass through the garden. He observed one stopping for a dip in the garden pool, highlighting the increasingly common overlap between wildlife and residential life in Los Angeles County, where housing developments have spread into bear habitat.
![A red-brown, speckled sea hare rests on the sandy seabed, surrounded by long green seaweed fronds.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/53f3/live/8cd3e190-8f14-11f1-a7ab-8b30adf0800a.jpg)
Title: Ocean Protector
Photographer: Ralph Pace (USA) - 2025 Underwater category winner
Category: Highly Commended, Wetlands: The Bigger Picture
Location: Monterey Bay, California, USA
A sea hare glides through an eelgrass meadow in the shallows of Monterey Bay, where Pace was photographing in the evening light. He saw the encounter as a hopeful image of "a gentle giant safeguarding the last green meadows of the sea".
By grazing on red algae, that can prevent sunlight reaching the meadow, sea hares play a role in restoring eelgrass, which is vital to coastal ecosystems and an important carbon sink.
![A stage performance featuring a large brown bear riding a small three-wheeled motorbike with two colourful nesting-doll props on the back, while a performer in a blue and white costume gestures toward them. A winter forest scene is projected on the screens behind them.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/cc13/live/92474c20-8f14-11f1-a7ab-8b30adf0800a.jpg)
Title: The Show Goes On
Photographer: Pietro Rojas (Guatemala)
Category: Highly Commended, Photojournalism
Location: Doha, Qatar
After learning that a circus featuring animal acts was in town, Rojas went to document it and saw a brown bear riding a small motorcycle, muzzled and secured to the apparatus. For him the scene highlighted the contrast between the animal's wild nature and the human environment imposed upon it.
More than 50 countries around the world have now banned or restricted the use of wild animals in circuses, over concerns it causes them distress, external.
Wildlife Photographer of the Year is developed and produced by the Natural History Museum, London.
summary: The article showcases a selection of highly commended images from the Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 competition, featuring remarkable animal behaviors and portraits from around the globe. The featured photographs capture diverse moments, such as a polar bear peering down a seal's breathing hole, an orca carrying a deceased calf, and a bullfrog narrowly missing a butterfly. Overall winners for the 2026 competition will be announced on October 13, 2026, followed by an exhibition at the Natural History Museum in London.
key_points: The Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 overall winners will be announced on October 13, 2026.
Photographer Audun Rikardsen captured a female polar bear looking down a seal's breathing hole using a rigged underwater camera.
Vegard Byrkjeland Aasen photographed an adult orca carrying a dead calf in a Norwegian fjord, a behavior currently under study.
An exhibition showcasing the competition's works will open at the Natural History Museum in London on October 16, 2026.

title: What Each Member Of The British Royal Family Reportedly Thinks About Harry & Meghan's UK Return - The List
author: Hannah Rice
content:
What Each Member Of The British Royal Family Reportedly Thinks About Harry & Meghan's UK Return
On August 19, 2026, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, announced that they would be returning to the U.K. after their shocking move to Montecito, California, six years earlier. By all accounts, the news caught many members of the royal family off guard, as Harry and Meghan previously been quite vocal about their distaste for royal life. As a result, the royals' annual summer gathering at Balmoral Castle has reportedly transformed from a fun family gathering into a series of crisis talks. Behind closed doors, King Charles III, Queen Camilla, Prince William, and other senior royals have apparently been discussing the impact of Harry and Meghan's return on the monarchy. But what are they saying?
According to some reports, members of the royal family are torn between their love for Harry and their disdain toward his behavior. For many palace higher-ups, the publication of Harry's dramatic tell-all memoir "Spare" was the ultimate betrayal. That said, Charles' cancer diagnosis has apparently made some view the king's estrangement with Harry in a new light. While there are members of the royal family who hope to see Charles reconcile with his beloved son, others wish to banish Harry from the royal milieu. Either way, Harry and Meghan's royal return won't be easy. As royal expert Joe Little told The Guardian after the news broke, it will take time for bridges to be rebuilt. "It's not going to be a case of six weeks and everything is forgiven and forgotten," Little said. "It's going to be a lengthy process."
King Charles III is apparently looking forward to more family time
Although King Charles III has certainly taken issue with Prince Harry's behaviors in the past, the monarch is reportedly looking forward to spending more time with the Sussex family as a whole. Following Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex's big move to the U.S. in 2020, Charles has not had many opportunities to spend time with the couple — or their children. Reports indicate that the king has particularly struggled in the absence of his grandchildren, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. King Charles has a special relationship with Princess Charlotte and her siblings, but he hasn't had a chance to build such a bond with Harry's kids. As royal expert Tom Quinn told Woman's Day in 2024, the king is "desperate" to spend more time with Archie and Lilibet and get a chance to create positive memories with them.
Charles, who reportedly learned of Harry and Meghan's plans only days before the news broke to the rest of the world, has apparently greeted the news of the Sussexes' U.K. return with open arms. As People shared following the big announcement, Charles is said to be excited to see more of Harry and Meghan's family. That said, Charles' team was sure to inform the publication that his relationship with the Sussexes would be private. As of this writing, Charles does not seem interested in cultivating a professional connection with Harry and Meghan.
The king may still have his reservations about Prince Harry
King Charles III is reportedly quite excited about the prospect of spending more time with his Sussex grandkids, but that doesn't mean that all is well. While Charles is prepared to welcome Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, back into his family, reports indicate that the king continues to harbor some reservations. According to a piece in The Times, Charles does not want Harry and Meghan to resume their previous duties as working royals. Apparently, he hopes to respect the position of his late mother, Queen Elizabeth II, regarding the couple's famous "half-in, half-out" proposition. In Charles' mind, it seems, royal commitment is an "all or nothing matter." Although Harry is his son, Charles is not willing to make exceptions.
Royal experts largely agree that Charles' stance is a prudent one. Speaking to The Times for the previously cited article, royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams explained that Charles cannot invest a lot of energy into the Sussexes at this time. Instead, Fitzwilliams argued, the monarch must focus on Prince William and Princess Catherine. "The Waleses are the future of the monarchy — both of them and their children — and that is also how the public see it, so there is only a certain amount that the king would be wise to give," the expert stated. At the end of the day, it seems Charles is expected to continue to offer his support to the family poised to succeed him.
Queen Camilla reportedly wants to proceed with caution
Like her husband, King Charles III, Queen Camilla is understood to feel hesitant about welcoming Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, back into the royal fold. On one hand, Camilla is believed to be thrilled about the possibility of building a relationship with Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. On the other, she reportedly harbors a clear distrust toward Meghan and Harry — the latter of whom referred to her as a "wicked stepmother" in his bombshell memoir, "Spare."
Chatting with the Australian outlet New Idea in July 2026, a royal insider claimed that Camilla's attitude toward the Sussexes has verged on suspicion. The source stated that, during a July 2026 tea with Harry and Meghan, Camilla expressed her concern about the couple's history of leaking stories to the press. Apparently, the queen's "true mission was to put Meghan in her place and establish a new set of rules should they continue renewing relations." Camilla apparently said that she wanted the chance to get to know Archie and Lilibet; however, she also set some serious boundaries. "She made it clear that this [family gathering] was for Archie and Lilibet, but if there were any leaks about their meeting, the door would be closed forever," the insider added.
Moving forward, it is thought that Camilla will maintain her position surrounding family meetings. She will want to spend time with the youngest Sussexes. That said, Camilla won't likely tolerate another tell-all.
Prince William is said to be livid at the news of Prince Harry's return
While King Charles III and Queen Camilla seem cautiously optimistic about Prince Harry's return to the U.K., Prince William is believed to be furious. The future King of England has long harbored resentment toward his younger brother, as evidenced by the timeline of Prince William and Prince Harry's feud. In William's eyes, Harry threatened the monarchy with the unflattering contents of the book "Spare." The Prince of Wales did not appreciate this attack on the institution that he has given his life to. Family friends told the BBC that William has taken Harry's betrayals very personally — and that he has no plans to forgive his younger brother. "William is very stubborn," one said. "To feel cheated by your own brother has been painful. He can't just put it behind him."
As William has grappled with the news of Harry's U.K. return, his closest friends have rallied behind him. In the same interview with the BBC, the previously mentioned unnamed source said, "This is a hard situation for him full of emotion and anger and we will support him." That said, some members of William's inner circle are worried about the way that Harry's big move might impact the quality of his work. "It is really important for me to ensure that any work we do with William will be focused on making a positive change and won't be affected by the Harry and Meghan drama," the friend added.
Rumor has it that Prince William is planning to give Prince Harry the silent treatment upon his return
Because of Prince William's negative feelings toward Prince Harry, the former does not necessarily have plans to speak to the latter upon his return to Britain. On the contrary, William may actually be planning to give Harry the silent treatment — because of the way that the Wales family was portrayed in "Spare." As one royal insider told RadarOnline, "His position is that he has nothing to say to Harry, and he has vowed he will not be drawn into meetings simply because Harry is living in the country again." Apparently, William will ice Harry out to the best of his ability, telling friends "he will not be speaking to either of [the Sussexes] for the foreseeable future."
Speaking to RadarOnline for the same report, the previously mentioned source said that William views Harry as a threat to his family. "There is still enormous anger on William's part over what was said about Catherine and the family [in Harry's tell-alls]. William sees protecting his wife and children as his priority," the insider shared. This is ultimately why King Charles and Prince William's relationship is believed to be in a fragile state over Prince Harry. William does not share his father's desire to forgive and forget. In the words of the same source, "Charles may want reconciliation with his younger son, but William is nowhere near that point and doesn't intend to pretend otherwise."
Princess Catherine reportedly feels overwhelmed by the news
Princess Catherine has not had an easy go of things. Since joining the royal family back in 2011, the Princess of Wales has overcome numerous challenges ranging from press harassment to a public cancer diagnosis. Given everything that Catherine has been through, royal experts believe that she has been feeling very overwhelmed by the news of Prince Harry's return to the U.K. As royal expert Christopher Andersen told Us Weekly after the Sussexes' the move was announced, "[William and Catherine] have so much on their plate as it is ... they don't really need to cope with having Harry and Megan on their proverbial doorstep."
Making matters worse, it's understood that neither Catherine nor her husband, Prince William, had any idea that Harry wanted to move back to England. The Sussex family's announcement apparently left both Catherine and William in a state of shock. "They're absolutely fuming to be blindsided like this but, like the king, there's nothing they can do about it," an inside source told Woman's Day. While Catherine may not be thrilled with the news, all she can do is try to move past it. The Princess of Wales remained famously calm in the wake of the publication of "Spare," and royal fans expect to see Catherine performing her royal duties as usual — even as Harry steps back into the spotlight.
The Wales camp is expected to go into crisis mode
Prince William and Princess Catherine are believed to be fairly united on the issue of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex's return to the U.K. Although many members of the royal family — namely King Charles III and Queen Camilla — apparently want to give Harry and Meghan another chance, the Waleses are another story. According to some reports, William and Catharine are worried that Harry and Meghan's big move might pose a risk to the monarchy. A source even told Woman's Day that the Waleses are trying to mitigate the crisis. "William's team are in intense meetings on how to minimize any risk to him and the family," the insider said. "He'll be seeking advice from everyone from lawyers to diplomatic-crisis experts."
William and Catherine are reportedly worried that Harry and Meghan may wish to return to their previous royal roles. As the previously cited insider told Woman's Day, "William suspects Harry and Meghan actually do think they're going to be accepted back onto the royal roster." For the Waleses, this may very well be a sort of worst-case scenario. "William's convinced this is their long game – and he's stunned that Harry thinks there would be even remotely a chance," they added. Regardless of Harry and Meghan's intentions, it sure seems that William and Catherine do not trust the couple. They will potentially remain in crisis mode as the Sussexes' move unfolds.
Princess Anne may want Prince Harry to mend his relationships
While the Wales camp has gone into full-blown crisis mode, Princess Anne has taken a totally different approach to Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex's return to Britain. As King Charles III's younger sister, Anne has reportedly developed quite a bit of empathy for his plight. Although she was displeased with Harry and Meghan's royal exit, Anne is also understood to empathize with Charles' desire to build a relationship with his Sussex grandchildren. As such, it seems that Anne wants to see a family reunion unfold.
Conversing with the Express, an anonymous source close to Anne said that she's eager to see the dust settle on Harry's feud with Prince William. She hopes that the brothers start channeling their energy into building bridges with their father, whose cancer diagnosis has greatly impacted his health. Per this source, Anne would like to play the role of peacemaker in the upcoming negotiations. However, she has apparently taken a strong stance against any future drama, telling Harry, "This nonsense has gone on far too long."
Whether William and Harry take Anne up on her peacemaking offer remains to be seen. Princess Anne's relationship with Harry and Meghan has not always been smooth sailing. That said, all signs point to Harry agreeing with his hard-working aunt. As the the spare heir told the BBC in 2025, "I would love reconciliation with my family. There's no point continuing to fight anymore, life is precious."
Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie are believed to be out of the loop
Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie have survived many royal scandals, but their relationships with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, have apparently not remained intact. Once upon a time, Harry and Meghan were close enough to the York princesses that they would have been thrilled with the duo's royal return. But, by 2023, it was clear that Prince Harry's royal rift was affecting Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie. By 2026, things between Harry and his York cousins had apparently reached a boiling point, and the trio quickly fell out of contact.
According to a piece in Hello!, Harry and Meghan have largely lost their connection with Beatrice and Eugenie. A source explained, "Beatrice and Eugenie are not even in touch [with the Sussexes] — and Eugenie was once so close to him." This distance seems quite strange, given that Harry and Meghan spent the summer of 2026 in Portugal, where Eugenie also has a home. Interestingly, the source also told Hello! that Harry and Eugenie did not connect during that period. As of this writing, it seems fair to assume Beatrice and Eugenie aren't going to be throwing the Sussexes any sort of homecoming party.
Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet are said to be thrilled with their parents' decision
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, sent shockwaves through the British royal family with their decision to return to the U.K. in 2026. As much as their choice has impacted the likes of King Charles III and Prince William, it has had an even greater effect on two of the youngest members of the Firm. Harry and Meghan's two children will trade their laid-back life in Montecito, California, for something a little bit more royal. This is expected to be a huge shock for the kids, as Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet reportedly had no idea that they were royals.
While Archie and Lilibet are poised to undergo a massive change in lifestyle, the two young royals are reportedly very excited about making the move. They are said to be particularly hopeful about the possibility of playing with Prince William and Princess Catherine's children — Prince George, Princess Charlotte, and Prince Louis. One inside source even told Woman's Day, "But what excites the kids more than anything, by all accounts, is that they'll finally have the chance to get to know their cousins." Of course, given all the negativity between William and Harry, it's hard to say when the kids will all connect. Despite these obstacles, the source noted, "It's been tough to be so far away and out of the loop from a family point of view."
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's announcement to return to the U.K. has triggered crisis talks among senior members of the British royal family. While King Charles III and Queen Camilla are cautiously open to spending time with their grandchildren under strict privacy and boundary rules, King Charles remains opposed to any return to working royal duties. Conversely, Prince William and Princess Catherine are reportedly furious, overwhelmed, and blindsided by the move, with William planning to give his brother the silent treatment.
key_points: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle announced their return to the U.K. after six years in California, surprising the royal family.
King Charles III is reportedly eager to spend time with his grandchildren, Archie and Lilibet, but opposes any return to working royal status for the couple.
Queen Camilla is willing to build a relationship with the younger Sussexes under strict boundaries to prevent media leaks.
Prince William is reportedly furious, feeling deeply betrayed by Harry's memoir, and intends to give him the silent treatment.
Princess Catherine and Prince William were blindsided by the news and are concerned the move poses a risk to the monarchy.

title: Kimmel stand-in Jelly Roll makes brutal dig at Trump’s weight gain
author: Tom Murray
content:
Rapper Jelly Roll took aim at Donald Trump’s weight during his guest hosting appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live! on Monday.
The “Need A Favor” star has famously trimmed down in recent years, going from a peak weight of around 540–550 pounds down to the mid-200s.
“A lot of doctors are worried about the president’s weight,” Jelly Roll said during his opening monologue on Kimmel’s show. “After his last physical, we found out Trump gained 14 pounds, which means he is now tipping the scales at almost 240. That’s crazy.”
He continued: “Think about this, y’all, in the last few years I’ve lost 300 pounds. That means I’ve lost an entire Donald Trump.
“And let’s be honest, based on his approval ratings, it seems like most of the country wants to do the same thing,” he joked.
![Jelly Roll urged Donald Trump to lose some weight during his guest hosting spot on ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/08/25/12/14/Jelly-Roll-and-Donald-Trump.jpeg)
It comes after The Washington Post reported this week that doctors have warned that weight gain is “a strong risk factor” for the president’s health after the commander-in-chief put on 23 pounds in three years.
Trump, a known lover of McDonald’s and Diet Coke, has long faced concerns about his overall health, including bruising on his hands and swelling of his ankles.
“We know that obesity is a strong risk factor for numerous health issues — as well as premature disability and death,” Dr. Scott Kahan, the director of the National Center for Weight and Wellness, told the Post. “Addressing obesity to protect the president’s health should be a priority similar to ensuring Secret Service protections for his life.”
Jelly Roll went on to suggest in his monologue that people “should take it easy” on the president about his weight, given that he “would never do that to other people.”
The broadcast then cut to show various clips of Trump making disparaging remarks about people’s bodies over the years.
The rapper responded: “Well, if that ain’t the pot calling the kettle fat.”
“Mr. President,” he quipped, “From one fat pig to another, take it from me that physical fitness is very important. And trust me, you’ll be happy to see your penis again.”
The Independent has contacted The White House for comment.
Trump and the White House have brushed off concerns about the aging president’s mental and physical acuity, often comparing his energy levels to that of his predecessor Joe Biden, whom Trump nicknamed “Sleepy Joe.”
“President Trump’s sharpness, unmatched energy, relentless work ethic and historic accessibility stand in stark contrast to what we saw during the last administration when Democrats and the legacy media intentionally covered up Joe Biden’s serious mental and physical decline from the American people,” White House spokesman Davis Ingle told the Post.
“President Trump is the sharpest and most accessible President in American history who is working nonstop to solve problems and deliver on his promises.”
summary: During his guest-hosting stint on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, rapper Jelly Roll mocked Donald Trump's recent weight gain during his opening monologue. The rapper compared Trump's weight to his own significant weight loss and highlighted health concerns recently reported by media outlets. Jelly Roll joked about Donald Trump gaining 14 pounds, noting his own substantial weight loss of 300 pounds.
Recent reports from The Washington Post highlighted doctors' warnings regarding the president's weight gain and health risks.

title: How Dolly Parton Helped Make Buffy the Vampire Slayer a Reality
author: Ray Flook
content:
Posted in: CW, Hulu, TV | Tagged: btvs, buffy, Dolly Parton
How Dolly Parton Helped Make Buffy the Vampire Slayer a Reality
We're looking back at how the late Dolly Parton helped make "Buffy the Vampire Slayer" a reality, and Sarah Michelle Gellar's thoughts.
Article Summary
- Dolly Parton helped make Buffy the Vampire Slayer happen through Sandollar Television, which co-produced all seven seasons.
- Parton and Sandy Gallin’s company backed Buffy from the film to TV, alongside Joss Whedon’s Mutant Enemy and Fox.
- Sarah Michelle Gellar said Dolly Parton was a “silent” Buffy producer whose praise meant everything to her.
- Parton stayed invested in Buffy’s future, later teasing a revival and helping keep Buffy Summers’ legacy alive.
Earlier today, the heartbreaking news hit that global icon and humanitarian Dolly Parton, known to the world as a beloved singer, songwriter, philanthropist, actress, playwright, and author, passed away at the age of 80. As the world honors the life she led and the lasting impact she continues to have on younger generations, we wanted to take a moment to remember the role she played in making the Sarah Michelle Gellar-starring Buffy the Vampire Slayer a reality. Parton and her former manager, Sandy Gallin, founded Sandollar Productions, and it was that production company's television division (Sandollar Television) that would go on to co-produce all seven seasons of "Buffy" as well as the David Boreanaz-starring spinoff series Angel.
Co-producing the original film with Kuzui Enterprises, the two production companies would join Joss Whedon's Mutant Enemy Productions and 20th Century Fox Television (now 20th Television) to develop the television series. To offer you a better perspective on just how much "The Queen" meant to her, Gellar discussed Parton being a "silent" producer on the series, how crucial Parton was in getting the series off the ground, how she reacted after Parton praised the series, and the moment when she realized that Parton knew who she was during a 2023 visit to NBC's The Tonight Show.
"Yes, little-known fact, the legend Dolly Parton was a producer. We never saw her [but] we'd get Christmas gifts in the beginning that would have our name, and I would think, 'She doesn't even know who I am.' And then one day, someone asked her about it, and she complimented the show and my performance. I was like, 'Oh, I can die now. Dolly Parton knows who I am and thinks I'm good,'" Gellar shared. It's a great moment, and it becomes clear early on how much of an inspiration Gellar was to her:
Parton's interest in bringing Buffy the Vampire Slayer continued into 2024, dropping news to Business Insider that "they're thinking about bringing it back and revamping it." Three months later, in April 2024, Gellar a return. Eventually, that would lead to the pilot for Gellar, Showrunners Nora Zuckerman and Lila Zuckerman, director and executive producer Chloé Zhao, and EP Gail Berman's Gellar and Ryan K. Armstrong-starring Buffy the Vampire Slayer: New Sunnydale. Though the project would end up moving forward, it's hard to believe that Buffy Summers won't be back on our screens down the road – and we have Parton to thank for helping make all of this a reality.

Star Sarah Michelle Gellar described Parton as a "silent" producer whose praise and support meant a great deal to her during the run of the series. Parton's production company initially backed the franchise from the original film to the television series alongside other partners.
key_points: Dolly Parton co-founded Sandollar Productions, whose television division co-produced all seven seasons of "Buffy the Vampire Slayer" and the spinoff "Angel."
Sarah Michelle Gellar referred to Dolly Parton as a "silent" producer who sent the cast Christmas gifts.
Gellar expressed deep admiration for Parton, noting that receiving praise from the music and entertainment icon meant everything to her.
Parton remained invested in the franchise, later discussing potential revamps and helping keep the legacy alive.

title: Police dig up huge stash of illegal drugs buried underground ahead of Creamfields festival
author: Liberty Dunworth
content:
Police have dug up a huge stash of illegal drugs buried underground ahead of Creamfields festival, just days before the festival kicks off.
Gates to the Cheshire festival open for the 2026 edition on Thursday (August 27), and it is expected to see over 80,000 fans visit across the weekend.
Local police have now revealed that they have found a huge stash of drugs buried at the festival site, including 204 canisters of laughing gas (nitrous oxide), and bags containing ketamine tablets, MDMA and ecstasy.
The drugs were found in a pre-event search of the grounds, and superintendent Andy Blizard shared a statement, saying that it has become a regular thing for punters to try and hide illegal drugs at the site ahead of the festival starting.
“Every year, we counter a number of brazen individuals who think they can outsmart us by concealing drugs from view or burying them at the site months in advance,” he shared (as per BBC News), adding that there is a “zero-tolerance policy regarding drugs”.
Police dig up buried stash of drugs in Creamfields grounds. Read more 👇https://t.co/DD8SDMoCpt pic.twitter.com/wGnBRjSI61
— Greatest Hits Radio Liverpool & North West News (@GHRLiverpool) August 24, 2026
The officer also clarified that there would be more searching of the site from police in the next few days, meaning that “many of those who chose to bury these items” will be “very much disappointed to find them no longer where they left them”.
Recommended
He also clarified that police will be onsite at Creamfields alongside security staff, and that anyone who would like to get back their rucksack that they buried should “get in contact with us”.
Artists on the Creamfields 2026 bill include Eric Prydz, Calvin Harris, Swedish House Mafia, Alesso, Martin Garrix, Tiësto and Disclosure.
This isn’t the first time that police have confirmed that they have found illegal drugs stashed ahead of a big music event. Back in 2024, addiction counsellors claimed that Oasis fans “stashed drugs” in Manchester’s Heaton Park ahead of the 2025 reunion shows.
At the time, drug and alcohol rehab facility Providence Project said that they had spoken to members of the addiction community, “who have told us they have already stashed drugs in the park”, adding they “would warn organisers to be vigilant.” They went on to say people had bragged about various plans to smuggle drugs into the show, including using glow sticks, toys, merchandise and plaster casts to conceal them.
Liam Gallagher also spoke about the news and gave a characteristically jovial response, saying: “I did it years ago when I went to see the pope in HP it’s not a new thing.”
summary: Police conducting a pre-event search discovered a large stash of illegal drugs buried underground at the Creamfields festival site in Cheshire. The seized items included laughing gas canisters, ketamine tablets, MDMA, and ecstasy ahead of the festival's Thursday opening. Authorities have a zero-tolerance policy for drugs and plan to conduct further searches of the grounds.
key_points: Police uncovered a buried stash of drugs at the Creamfields festival site ahead of its Thursday opening.
The seized drugs included 204 canisters of laughing gas, ketamine tablets, MDMA, and ecstasy.
Superintendent Andy Blizard stated that police maintain a zero-tolerance policy regarding illegal drugs.
Authorities plan to conduct additional searches of the festival grounds in the coming days.

title: Only Murders In The Building Season 6 is heading to London — and we know when it hits Disney+
author: Jordan King
content:
Between the likes of The Thursday Murder Club, Ludwig, and Death Valley, cosy crime dramas are having something of a moment just now. But regardless of the murder mystery movies and shows vying for our eyeballs of late, six seasons in, Disney+ and Hulu's Only Murders In The Building remains the undisputed GOAT of the genre. And with Charles, Oliver, and Mabel's next outing set to take the crime solving podcaster trio away from the Arconia and across the pond to London, Disney+ has today confirmed an 8 December release date for OMITB Season 6 — and dropped a few first-look pictures from the season ahead. Check them out below;
![Only Murders In The Building Season 6](https://images.bauerhosting.com/empire/2026/08/182551_0502R2.jpg?auto=format&w=1440&q=80)
![Only Murders In The Building Season 6](https://images.bauerhosting.com/empire/2026/08/182292_0696R2.jpg?auto=format&w=1440&q=80)
![Only Murders In The Building Season 6](https://images.bauerhosting.com/empire/2026/08/182551_0141R2.jpg?auto=format&w=1440&q=80)
![Only Murders In The Building Season 6](https://images.bauerhosting.com/empire/2026/08/182555_0081R2.jpg?auto=format&w=1440&q=80)
![Only Murders In The Building Season 6](https://images.bauerhosting.com/empire/2026/08/1825500107R2-668392c.jpg.webp?auto=format&w=1440&q=80)
Well there you have it — that's certainly Steve Martin, Martin Short, and Selena Gomez in a variety of locations that look distinctly like London! But arguably, it's who we don't see here that should have you really excited for Only Murders' return, because the gang's trip to Blighty is bringing with it one hell of an ensemble of Britain and Ireland's finest to bolster the victim/suspect line-up. For those who didn't already know, OMITB Season 6's role call includes *deep breath* Olivia Colman, Nicola Coughlan, Martin Freeman, Sharon Horgan, Jim Broadbent, Jennifer Saunders, Geri Halliwell, Sean Teale, Simone Ashley, Rhea Norwood, Richard Ayoade, Jamie Demetriou, Derek Jacobi, Kathryn Hunter, Lesley Nicol and not one, not two, but three Doctors in the form of Peter Capaldi, David Tennant, and Jodie Whittaker. Yeah, we're thinkin' that's one hell of a line-up!
The official synopsis for Only Murders In The Building Season 6 — which will also see the returns of series regulars Meryl Streep and Tina Fey — reads as follows: "In Season 6, after successfully bringing the guilty to justice once again, our trio Charles (Steve Martin), Oliver (Martin Short) and Mabel (Selena Gomez) embark on their hardest case yet when the next victim — Cinda Canning — arrives at their doorstep, summoning them to London to catch her killer. Our beloved trio of true crime-solving podcasters must now navigate their way through the home of the cozy murder mystery, replete with a whole new collection of suspicious and particularly English-eccentric characters. But can they follow in the footsteps of the woman whose podcast started it all for them … without having their story end the same as hers?"
London awaits. There's another murder to be solved. And co-creators Martin and John Hoffman have the most who's-who-iest (and Who-iest) of whodunits on their hands for us this time out. So sharpen your pencils, dust off your magnifying glasses, and crack open a fresh moleskin for Only Murders In The Building Season 6's return on 8 December. It's shaping up to be a real killer...
summary: Disney+ has confirmed an December 8 release date for Season 6 of Only Murders In The Building, which will take podcasting trio Charles, Oliver, and Mabel to London. In the new season, the detectives face their hardest case yet when podcast rival Cinda Canning arrives at their doorstep as a victim, summoning them to England. The upcoming season features a massive ensemble cast of British and Irish actors alongside returning series regulars.
key_points: Season 6 of Only Murders In The Building premieres on December 8 on Disney+.
The plot takes Charles, Oliver, and Mabel away from the Arconia and to London to solve a new case involving Cinda Canning.
The guest cast includes notable actors such as Olivia Colman, Nicola Coughlan, Martin Freeman, and three former Doctors: Peter Capaldi, David Tennant, and Jodie Whittaker.
Series regulars Meryl Streep and Tina Fey are also set to return for the new season.

title: 'Strictly Come Dancing's Giovanni Pernice Suicidal After BBC Exit
author: Jake Kanter
content:
![Giovanni Pernice will not appear on BBC show 'Strictly Come Dancing' this  year.](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/ba17fa200b39-giovanni-pernice.jpg?w=681&h=383&crop=1) 
Professional dancer Giovanni Pernice has vented his fury at the BBC over its handling of his Strictly Come Dancing exit following a clash with Sherlock star Amanda Abbington.
In an interview with The Daily Telegraph, Pernice said he was left feeling suicidal after being “hung out to dry” by the BBC, arguing that the broadcaster’s duty of care did not extend to him.
Pernice has not appeared on Strictly (the format on which Dancing with the Stars is based) since 2023, when he clashed with dance partner Abbington, who later filed a complaint.
Watch on Deadline
Abbington alleged that her Italian dance partner was “nasty” and accused him of inappropriate bullying behavior during her five weeks on Strictly.
The BBC’s subsequent investigation partially upheld some of her concerns, though the corporation was never specific about the nature of the allegations it deemed credible. The BBC apologized to Abbington for her experience on Strictly, which remains one of the UK’s most-watched shows.
“I feel they hung me out to dry to cover their backs. I was devastated by that,” Pernice said in an excerpt from his memoir, Gio: Taking the Lead, published by The Telegraph.
He added that BBC’s apology “made it seem like all of the stories in the newspaper[s] were real, when most of them had been found to be totally untrue. Her claims had ruined my life and my career. Where was my apology?”
He told The Telegraph: “I had made concerted efforts to be positive and supportive to Amanda, in both the training room and our text conversations.” He claimed that most of the upheld complaints related to him swearing: “They found that I threw my arms up and said ‘f***’ on one occasion.”
Pernice said he should never have been paired with Abbington. “I’m a taskmaster,” he said. “But I know that I can take you to the final, and that I can take you to win the show – if you want to be pushed.”
Pernice found himself “spiralling mentally” following the controversy. “I’m a very work-oriented person,” he said. “I really dedicate my life to work. It wasn’t even the financial [side]. It’s more, I have to do something. I always wanted to be something.
“I was thinking, ‘There’s no place for me any more in this industry. So what’s the point?’ That’s when I thought, ‘Well, let’s end this. There’s no point. Let’s end it. I’m never going to have back what I had.’”
On the BBC’s response, he added: “They didn’t look after me. ‘Well, you’re not contracted with us, your contract finished in December.’ Yeah, but I’ve been with you for nine years, so you can look after me. If I’m sending an email saying that I’ve got myocarditis and depression, you can’t even reply to me and say, ‘Oh, sorry if you feel a bit down’?”
The BBC has been approached for comment.
summary: Professional dancer Giovanni Pernice stated in an interview that he felt suicidal and abandoned by the BBC following his exit from 'Strictly Come Dancing'. His departure stemmed from a dispute with former dance partner Amanda Abbington, who accused him of inappropriate behavior. An internal BBC investigation partially upheld some of Abbington's complaints, leading the broadcaster to issue an apology.
key_points: Giovanni Pernice expressed feeling suicidal and hung out to dry by the BBC after his exit from Strictly Come Dancing.
The controversy followed a complaint by former dance partner Amanda Abbington, who alleged bullying behavior during her time on the show.
A BBC investigation partially upheld some of Abbington's concerns and the corporation issued her an apology.
Pernice stated that the situation ruined his life and career, while claiming that most upheld complaints related to him swearing on a single occasion.

title: Ali G is back: Sacha Baron Cohen returns in trailer for Ali G: Who Iz I? movie sequel
author: Ben Travis
content:
In the late ‘90s and early ‘00s, Ali G was a sensation. If he’s since been overtaken by Borat in terms of cultural ubiquity, he was once Sacha Baron Cohen’s most famous character – from Da Ali G Show, to 2002’s big-screen outing Ali G Indahouse, and even appearing in Madonna’s ‘Music’ music video. But it’s been a decade since Ali G last made an appearance, at the 2016 Oscars (a secret until Cohen literally stepped on stage in the role) – and now, he’s back to trouble Hollywood once more. Ali G: Who Iz I? is the official sequel movie, 24 years after Indahouse, and the first trailer is here.
Word of an Ali G sequel emerged earlier this year when Cohen was spotted filming as the character, and the shroud of secrecy was officially dropped when he showed up at the Wimbledon’s Men’s finals this summer. The sequel – directed by Cohen himself, his directorial debut – sees Ali G back to cause more mayhem, while also pondering his own existence in the face of impending fatherhood with his girlfriend Julie (Morgana Robinson). Though, any narrative is really just an excuse for the character to wreak havoc on an unsuspecting public. Who Iz I? arrives six years after Cohen returned as Borat for sequel Borat Subsequent Moviefilm.
Does Ali G still work as a character in 2026? Will the film prove just as worthwhile as the surprisingly decent second movie Borat movie? And will he be menacing Madonna again? We’ll find out when Ali G: Who Iz I? hits cinemas on October 23.
summary: Sacha Baron Cohen is returning as his iconic character Ali G in a new sequel movie titled Ali G: Who Iz I?, set for release on October 23, 2026. The film marks Cohen's directorial debut and follows Ali G as he faces impending fatherhood with his girlfriend Julie while causing public mayhem. This official sequel arrives 24 years after the original Ali G Indahouse and a decade after the character's last appearance at the 2016 Oscars.
key_points: Sacha Baron Cohen is returning as Ali G in the official sequel movie, Ali G: Who Iz I?
The film features Cohen in his directorial debut as Ali G deals with impending fatherhood and wreaks havoc.
The sequel arrives 24 years after 2002's Ali G Indahouse and follows Cohen's 2020 Borat sequel.
Ali G: Who Iz I? is scheduled to hit cinemas on October 23, 2026.

title: Dolly Parton, country star, actor and philanthropist, dies aged 80
author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
content:
Dolly Parton, one of the greatest singer-songwriters in country music who was also much cherished for her philanthropy, has died aged 80.
Her death was announced by nephew Brian Seaver on Instagram. “I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven’t truly felt it until now,” he said. “It is an honour, an honour that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness.”
So gifted that she wrote two of the 20th century’s greatest songs – Jolene and I Will Always Love You – in a single day, Parton’s songwriting was characterised by its vivid storytelling, emotional acuity and melodic strength, all sung with strident clarity. From an eventual catalogue of hundreds of songs, she scored a record 25 US country No 1 singles and 47 albums in the country Top 10 . She crossed over into the pop charts with 9 to 5, a US No 1 in 1980; balanced her music career with acclaimed acting, twice earning Golden Globe nominations for her roles; and her Imagination Library literacy scheme donated more than 150m books to children.
This was all done with considerable panache, rhinestoned glamour and towering hairdos, with her immortal assertion regarding her appearance – “it takes a lot of money to look this cheap” – the most quoted example of Parton’s ready wit.
Parton was born in poverty in a one-room cabin in Tennessee, the fourth child to a mother who would have 12 children by the age of 35, and a father who was a farmer and construction worker. One of her best-loved songs, Coat of Many Colours, was about her mother creating patchwork clothes; Parton’s first guitar was cobbled together from a mandolin with bass guitar strings. Her first proper guitar was given to her aged eight by her uncle, and she went from singing in church, to appearing on local television aged 10, to cutting her first record aged 13. That year she appeared at the Grand Ole Opry, the concert hall in Nashville at the centre of country music, and her performance was introduced by Johnny Cash. “I’ve always believed things would go well, and I dreamed that they would even before I was in high school,” she later said. “I always wanted to be a star. It just seemed natural to me.”
![Dolly Parton in 1976](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b8594247774506db5c21757de7ef64352b123c1c/0_414_2730_2183/master/2730.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
After graduating high school in 1964 she moved to Nashville and started out as a songwriter rather than performer. The following year she was signed as an artist and initially moulded as a pop singer, without success; after she was allowed to switch to country, she scored back-to-back hits and released her debut album Hello, I’m Dolly. In 1966 she married Carl Dean – who died in 2025, with the couple renewing their vows in 2016 to mark 50 years together.
Beginning in 1967, a duet partnership with country singer and TV personality Porter Wagoner helped her star continue to ascend, and she had her first country No 1 in 1971 with the song Joshua.
Jolene, her unforgettably raw and desperate plea to a rival lover, was released in 1973 and became her first UK success, reaching No 7. I Will Always Love You, written to Wagoner as a farewell after their creative partnership, was a country No 1 in 1974 and again via a re-recorded version in 1982, and would go on to be a huge pop success when revived by Whitney Houston for the soundtrack of The Bodyguard in 1992: it is still the bestselling single of all time by a woman, with an estimated 20m sales.
In the mid 1970s Parton broadened her sound, embracing pop-rock arrangements on songs such as 1977’s Light of a Clear Blue Morning – its accompanying album New Harvest … First Gathering was her first entry in the pop album chart. Later that year its follow-up Here You Come Again reached the Top 20 and was her first million-selling LP, powered in part by its hit title track, which also won Parton the first of her 10 Grammy awards.
1980 was a peak in her success, with three back-to-back country No 1s, including 9 to 5, taken from the film of the same name which Parton starred in alongside Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin, earning her an Oscar nomination for best original song. Parton would later write songs for a stage musical version of 9 to 5, in 2008.
Another classic single came in 1983: Islands in the Stream, a duet with Kenny Rogers, which topped the US pop charts, and a Christmas album with Rogers in 1984 went two times platinum. There were more notable film roles in the 1980s, too, opposite Burt Reynolds in the The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas, Sylvester Stallone in Rhinestone, and an all-star female ensemble in Steel Magnolias.
after newsletter promotion
![Linda Ronstadt, Dolly Parton and Emmylou Harris in 1987.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b2965ca780b959d5d8c883074bb1afaee546ab9c/0_703_2319_2897/master/2319.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
A landmark Parton album came in 1987 with Trio, an exquisitely harmonised, springwater-clear collaboration with Emmylou Harris and Linda Ronstadt, earning Parton her only nomination for album of the year at the Grammys. Another all-star trio recording came in 1993, with Tammy Wynette and Loretta Lynn on the album Honky-Tonk Angels, followed by a reunion with Harris and Ronstadt from Trio II in 1999, featuring a Grammy-winning cover of Neil Young’s After the Gold Rush.
The turn of the century brought a trilogy of acclaimed bluegrass albums, and Parton would release 10 more LPs, the most recent being Rockstar in 2023. She was courted by a younger generation of stars, appearing with country artists such as Brad Paisley as well as pop singers such as Kesha, and her goddaughter Miley Cyrus. There were fewer acting roles, but she lent her voice to animated film Gnomeo and Juliet in 2011 and the following year appeared alongside Queen Latifah and more in musical film Joyful Noise.
Alongside her music and acting, Parton was an astute businesswoman and philanthropist. She founded the film and TV production company Sandollar, with former manager Sandy Gallin, which went on to produce hits such as Buffy the Vampire Slayer and the Father of the Bride film series. In 1986, she took a stake in the Silver Dollar City theme park in Tennessee and renamed it Dollywood, doubling its size over the next two decades, and a Dollywood-branded spa, cabin complex, theatre-restaurant concept and waterpark have since been opened.
![Dolly Parton in Joyful Noise](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/087bae255ca92a96d082798a05a74465f6c52df6/125_0_1250_1001/master/1250.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The Dollywood Foundation, funded through these business ventures and creative projects, was created in 1988, initially awarding college scholarships and running a scheme to help children complete high school in her native Sevier County, Tennessee. In 1995 Parton began her Imagination Library project, which sent an age-appropriate book to every child in the county every month until they were five. “My father could not read and write, and I saw how crippling that could be,” she explained. It expanded nationwide in 2000, internationally in 2006, and nearly 25m books are now distributed each year across the US, Canada, Australia, the UK and Ireland.
In 2022, Jeff Bezos donated $100m (£83m) to the foundation. That year, Parton explained that as well as improving child literacy, “it’s the fact they get recognised. They get this little book with their little name on it in the mail, and they feel special. They start taking pride in themselves, and they know that somebody out there is thinking of [them].”
![Dolly Parton receiving the Moderna vaccine she helped to fund.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/29a578dec171181a66c3c89920b1f58b99640a83/0_0_3500_2519/master/3500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Parton has also set up a reserve in 2003 to help preserve the bald eagle; contributed $500,000 to the opening of a Sevier county hospital in 2006; coordinated relief efforts for those affected by the Smoky mountain wildfires of 2016; and contributed to an HIV/Aids charity album. She supported Black Lives Matter and transgender rights, opposing a North Carolina “bathroom bill” that restricted transgender people’s access to toilets (Parton was also nominated for an Oscar for her song in trans drama Transamerica, entitled Travelin’ Thru).
She made a number of donations to Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, where her niece was treated for leukaemia. The most high profile of these was in 2020, when she donated $1m for research into Covid-19, which formed the basis for the eventual Moderna vaccine.
In May 2026, Parton cancelled her Las Vegas residency over health issues. A Broadway musical is also set to open later this year after a run in Nashville.
summary: Dolly Parton, the legendary country singer-songwriter, actor, and philanthropist, has died at the age of 80. Known for iconic hits like "Jolene" and "I Will Always Love You," she achieved a record 25 US country number-one singles and built a successful career spanning music, film, and business. Beyond her entertainment career, she was widely celebrated for her extensive philanthropy, including her Imagination Library literacy scheme and donations to medical research.
key_points: Dolly Parton passed away at the age of 80.
She wrote hundreds of songs, scoring a record 25 US country number-one singles and releasing dozens of albums.
Her musical success included crossover pop hits like "9 to 5" and writing "I Will Always Love You," later a massive hit for Whitney Houston.
She was an acclaimed actor, receiving Golden Globe and Oscar nominations.
Her extensive philanthropy included the Imagination Library literacy program, which has donated millions of books to children globally.

title: Russian stadium says it will not host Kanye concerts – but promoter says shows have not been cancelled
author: Laura Snapes
content:
The St Petersburg stadium that was set to host two concerts by Ye – making the rapper formerly known as Kanye West the biggest western act to play in Russia since start of the Ukraine war – has now said that the concerts will not take place at the venue, although the promoter has stressed that they have not been cancelled.
Gazprom Arena had previously posted on social media saying that “the most influential musical artist of our time” would perform there on 10 and 11 October. “This is no joke!” the post stated. The event sold out immediately, including tickets priced at £1390 ($1896).
The news came after countries including the UK, Italy, Poland, Switzerland, France and more blocked or sought to block concerts by Ye owing to public safety concerns over his prior antisemitic outbursts and expressions of sympathy towards nazism. In January, Ye issued an apology for his behaviour and discussed his mental health struggles. “I am not a Nazi or an antisemite,” he wrote. “I love Jewish people.”
The Russian venue has now released a statement distancing itself from the concerts. “In light of the numerous inquiries received by Gazprom Arena regarding the organisation of a Kanye West concert, we hereby officially state: Gazprom arena was not, and is not, the organiser of this event. That role was handled by the Moscow-based concert agency Say Agency.
“Gazprom Arena has not signed any contracts to lease the stadium for this event. No such contract exists. Consequently, the concert cannot take place at our venue.”
On Telegram, Say Agency said that it was surprised by the announcement, learning the news at the same time as the public, but that “as of now, the Ye concert has not been cancelled”.
Say Agency said that it announced the concerts after Gazprom arena approved an “official letter”, but said that the rental contract had not yet been signed ahead of its expiry later this week.
The planned appearance has caused controversy outside Russia. Ye’s plan to play the country – following in the footsteps of Paul Oakenfold, DaBaby, Jason Derulo and Akon – flouts sweeping sanctions and calls for culture boycotts.
Within Russia, politician Nikolay Novichkov called for the musician to be investigated for praising Hitler and said that the concerts should be cancelled unless he publicly declared “moral support for Russia and the special military operation”. Legislator Vitaly Milonov said Ye should perform traditional Russian songs at the planned concerts. “Maybe after this he’ll stop his disgusting antics and become a normal person,” he added.
Say Agency previously released a statement acknowledging the controversy. “Not everything Kanye West said should be forgotten. Many people are talking about Kanye today. Many are trying to criticise him for words spoken during difficult times. But it’s easy to judge based on a single statement. It’s more difficult to listen to a person who has been changing the industry for decades. We listened, and we want to remind you.”
Despite the controversy, fans have been undeterred from seeing Ye live when concerts have been allowed to proceed. He has recently performed to vast audiences in the US, Turkey, the Netherlands, Georgia, Albania, Portugal and Kazakhstan, with more dates planned for the US and Indonesia. The dates come in support of his 12th solo album, Bully, released in March.
summary: The Gazprom Arena in St Petersburg announced it will not host upcoming concerts by the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, stating no lease contract was signed. However, the concert promoter, Say Agency, insisted that the shows have not been cancelled. The planned event has drawn controversy internationally due to previous public safety concerns over the rapper's past behavior, and internally from Russian politicians calling for investigations or specific conditions.
key_points: Gazprom Arena stated it has no contract to host Kanye West and is not the event organizer.
Promoter Say Agency expressed surprise at the venue's announcement but maintained the concerts are not cancelled.
The planned shows have sparked controversy abroad regarding sanctions and boycotts, and within Russia where some politicians called for investigations or conditions.
Tickets for the St Petersburg dates had sold out immediately prior to the venue's statement.

title: James Blunt addresses claims he was 'very famous' man in dark Hayden Panettiere story
author: Isobel Lewis
content:
James Blunt addresses claims he was 'very famous' man in dark Hayden Panettiere story
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Hayden Panettiere’s mother brands account of star’s final hours ‘full of holes’](<https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/25/10/24/Untitled-design-(10).png?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75>)
![The Weekender](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_weekender_embed_desktop.png)
Following the passing of the Heroes star, who died aged 36 on 16 August, there has been a renewed interest in Panettiere’s recent memoir This Is Me: A Reckoning and the many shocking stories she told in it.
In one portion of the book, Panettiere wrote about a trusted friend coaxing her to go downstairs in a yacht cabin, where they found “a famous thirty-something British singer-songwriter lying in a bed”, who was “undressed”.
After fans began to speculate online that Blunt was the man in question, the “You’re Beautiful” singer, 52, responded on Monday by sharing a Substack post to X titled: “Hayden Panettiere and James Blunt – An Internet Lynching” that “debunked” the rumours.
In the piece, journalist Dean Piper writes about a story he penned in 2009 about Panettiere and Blunt being “flirty” at the amfAR charity event in Cannes and being photographed on a boat together the next day.
“It only takes the smallest of AI searches to find out that in May 2009, when the pictures of Blunt and Panettiere were taken, she was 19, almost 20. So, if the incident happened when she was 18, Blunt’s not your guy to start with,” Piper wrote.
“And as she says she hadn’t met the man before the incident, and that she fled the boat immediately after, it takes nothing to work out that the cabin incident was the first and last time she met the man.
“So, pictures of Blunt and Panettiere at the amfAR charity event and together on the boat again the next day mean only one thing – he’s really not your man.”
Blunt reshared Piper’s story in seeming agreement on X, adding an emoji of two eyes looking to the side.
The Standard has contacted Blunt’s representatives for further comment.
In her book, Panettiere claimed that the friend had told her the man in question had a “huge d***” and told her to get into bed with him.
“He was shirtless and propped up on a few pillows with his arms positioned behind his head. From the waist down, he was covered by bedsheets, and I could see the outline of his body underneath,” she wrote.
![Hayden Panettiere died aged 36 on August 16 (PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/24/14/9791fa2523e762d633c8a00bff9cc652Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg3NjYwMjQz-2.20738992.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
“I could feel my heart pounding, as I settled in underneath the sheets, I disassociated. My body no longer felt like my own. The shock was so great it didn’t even occur to me to say no.”
Read More
Once the friend left, Panettiere says that she told the singer “this is not going to happen”, fled the room and left the boat.
Discussing the “horrifying” incident in her final interview before her death, Panettiere told podcaster Jay Shetty: “There was no jumping off and swimming away... I realised that there was nobody who was going to be empathetic to my situation, that this was nothing new to them.”
summary: Singer James Blunt has addressed online speculation linking him to an unsettling story from Hayden Panettiere's memoir, *This Is Me: A Reckoning*. In her book, Panettiere described an incident involving an undressed British singer-songwriter on a yacht. Blunt responded by sharing a Substack article that debunked the rumours using a timeline of events and past photographs.
key_points: Hayden Panettiere's memoir described an incident where a trusted friend led her to find an undressed British singer in a yacht cabin.
Following online speculation naming James Blunt as the man, Blunt shared a Substack post by journalist Dean Piper on X to debunk the rumors.
The debunking piece pointed out age and timeline discrepancies from a 2009 event, proving the dates did not match Panettiere's account.
Panettiere wrote that she fled the room and left the boat after telling the singer the encounter was not going to happen.

title: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Trailer: Sacha Baron Cohen’s Prankster Returns in Stunt Documentary
author: James Hibberd
content:
!['Ali G: Who Iz I?'](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Ali-G.png?crop=6px%2C0px%2C2822px%2C1580px&resize=2000%2C1126) 
The first trailer for Sacha Baron Cohen‘s latest top-secret movie project has been revealed.
Amazon-MGM Studios released the first footage from Ali G: Who Iz I? (below), which returns Cohen’s hip-hop journalist character in a feature film “documentary” following Cohen as he unleashes Ali G on an unsuspecting public.
“I’ve been gone for 20 years, chilling,” Cohen narrates as Ali G. “And in that time, the world went to crap. There’s been Wars. Covid. And Ed Sheeran. I’m going to get back on top with a brand new thing called a ‘documentary.’ For the first time ever, this is with real people not actors. For more than a year we let the cameras follow me everywhere. Nothing was off limits.”
Related Stories
![Sacha Baron Cohen in 'Ali G Indahouse'](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-hollywoodreporter-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
![Sacha Baron Cohen at Wimbledon on July 11, 2026.](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-hollywoodreporter-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
The footage includes Cohen’s taking classes, walking the streets, and going on various shows as Ali G (occasionally accompanied by a very pregnant-looking girlfriend, played by British comedian Morgana Robinson).
“It got the very latest firearms technology, action, drama, heartbreak, plot twists and the very latest TikTok trends,” Cohen adds.
The film marks Cohen’s directorial debut. The official description: “After twenty years spent ‘chillin’, tokin’ and bonin’,’ Ali G is shocked to discover that his long-term girlfriend, Julie, is 8 months pregnant. Faced with an extra mouth to feed, he gets off his batty and heads to America to reclaim his former glory… but soon encounters adversaries who will ultimately threaten his and his child’s very existence.
News first leaked that Cohen would be making another Ali G project in July and he was spotted in character attending Wimbledon.
Cohen first introduced Ali G on Channel 4’s The 11 O’Clock Show in 1998. Two years later, Cohen got his own series, Da Ali G Show, a sketch comedy series that included the character. Cohen also had a 2002 feature, Ali G Indahouse, but it was another Ali G Show character, Borat Sagdiyev, who would propel Cohen to global fame with the release of 2006’s Borat and its 2020 sequel Borat Subsequent Moviefilm.
Ali G: Who Iz I? will be released in theaters Oct. 23.
