title: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Trailer: Sacha Baron Cohen Returns as the London Bad Boy in New Amazon MGM Mockumentary
author: Jack Dunn
content:
Amazon MGM has released the official trailer for “Ali G: Who Iz I?,” a new mockumentary following Sacha Baron Cohen’s swaggering London bad boy.
“After 20 years spent chillin’, tokin’ and bonin’, Ali G is shocked to discover that his long-term girlfriend, Julie (Morgana Robinson), is eight months pregnant,” its official synopsis reads. “Faced with an extra mouth to feed, he gets off his batty and heads to America to reclaim his former glory… but soon encounters adversaries who will ultimately threaten his and his child’s very existence.”
Cohen first developed the titular character as part of Channel 4’s “The 11 O’Clock Show” in 1998 before getting his own series, “Da Ali G Show,” in the early 2000s. 2002 brought the release of the first Ali G movie, “Ali G Indahouse,” which was helmed by “Succession” director Mark Mylod.
Popular on Variety
Cohen filmed “Who Iz I?” in secret, just like he did with “Borat,” “Brüno” and his TV series “Who Is America?” Cohen’s brand of comedy revolves around him embodying outlandish characters and then provoking a reaction from onlookers. As Ali G, he’s interviewed Noam Chomsky, Andy Rooney and Newt Gingrich.
The three-time Oscar nominee unveiled the project in a video posted to his Instagram in July. In character as Ali G, he captioned the post, “Dey haz finally made a documentary about me. And it ain’t dat crap one about da penguins, dis one haz got at least twice as much animal sex.”
The film marks Cohen’s directorial debut, and he also serves as writer and producer under his Four by Two Films Banner. Petr Jákl and Emily Kob are executive producers.
Outside of his own films, Cohen recently played the villainous Mephisto on the Marvel Disney+ series “Ironheart.” He also starred in “Ladies First” for Netflix and “Balls Up” for Prime Video.
“Ali G: Who Iz I?” hits theaters on Oct. 23. Check out the trailer below.
summary: Amazon MGM has released the official trailer for "Ali G: Who Iz I?," a new mockumentary starring Sacha Baron Cohen as his iconic London bad boy character. In the film, Ali G discovers his girlfriend is eight months pregnant and travels to America to make money, facing adversaries that threaten his and his child's existence. The project marks Cohen's directorial debut and is scheduled to hit theaters on October 23.
key_points: Amazon MGM released the official trailer for the mockumentary "Ali G: Who Iz I?."
The plot follows Ali G traveling to America to provide for his unborn child after discovering his girlfriend is eight months pregnant.
The film marks Sacha Baron Cohen's directorial debut, where he also serves as writer and producer.
"Ali G: Who Iz I?" is scheduled to be released in theaters on October 23.

title: Irish actress Evanna Lynch marries fiancé in London
author: RTÉ Entertainment
content:
Co Louth actress Evanna Lynch, best known for starring in the Harry Potter film franchise, tied the knot with Denis Skinner last week.
The 35-year-old, famous for her role as Luna Lovegood in the popular fantasy film franchise, married her partner of almost five years in an intimate ceremony in London on Friday, according to British Vogue.
The couple had met in a pub in London two years prior, where the Frenchman was working as a bartender.
Lynch made her film debut in Harry Potter And The Order Of The Phoenix in 2007, but long before she stepped into her role as eccentric witch Luna she was pen pals with author JK Rowling.
The actress was battling an eating disorder at the time and wrote to Rowling about her own insecurities and struggles.
Lynch has continued to pursue acting since the Harry Potter series ended in 2011 and has featured in films such as My Name Is Emily and G.B.F. and made TV appearances in Sinbad and Dragon Striker.
The star consulted an astrologist to help with the wedding planning and eventually scheduled the event for 21 August 21 as her desired date on 22 August was unavailable, and because she was advised to avoid the solar eclipse.
![HAMBURG, GERMANY - SEPTEMBER 01: Evanna Lynch during the Harry Potter "Back to Hogwarts" Fan Event at Mehr! Theater am Großmarkt on September 1, 2024 in Hamburg, Germany. (Photo by Tristar Media/Getty Images)](https://www.rte.ie/images/0024e508-614.jpg?ratio=0.67) 
"I can totally see why. Lots of my friends have been sick, or a family member has died - it's been very dramatic," Lynch told the fashion magazine.
Lynch wore a vintage skirt her stylist found weeks before her wedding day, which she paired with a Moira Hughes corset from Ellie Sanderson to create her dream dress.
Her new husband opted for green corduroy tailoring from Suit Supply which he paired with shoes from Rothy’s, which were crafted from plastic bottles to reflect his environmentalism.
"A lot of people questioned wearing corduroy in August but Den would not be deterred," Lynch said.
The actress described the ceremony at Islington Town Hall in London as "very sweet and simple", and Vogue shared pictures of the happy couple accompanied by their dog Malo on the big day.
Lynch told the magazine: "When we started the wedding planning process, I was a bit disparaging of it all.
"It’s so over the top. It’s so lavish. But as we’ve gotten closer to it, I’ve realised how unique and special it is."
Other pictures from the day include snaps of the happy couple embracing, as well as pictures of the newlyweds during their reception at Wilton’s Music Hall - where they hired a swing band "to get people dancing".
Lynch also recounted getting engaged in 2023 and told the magazine she "totally knew" Skinner was going to pop the question after he originally asked her to marry him during a "big argument".
The publication wrote that Skinner planned a "private engagement surrounded by nature" in August later that year, around the date of her 32nd birthday.
The couple had met in a pub in London two years prior, where the Frenchman was working as a bartender.
Source: Press Association
If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this article, please see RTÉ's list of helplines
summary: Irish actress Evanna Lynch, best known for playing Luna Lovegood in the Harry Potter films, married her partner Denis Skinner in an intimate ceremony in London. The couple, who have been together for nearly five years, celebrated their wedding at Islington Town Hall and Wilton’s Music Hall. Lynch wore a custom gown combining a vintage skirt and a Moira Hughes corset, while Skinner wore eco-friendly green corduroy tailoring.
key_points: Evanna Lynch married Denis Skinner in an intimate London ceremony on Friday.
The couple met in a London pub where Skinner was working as a bartender.
Lynch is best known for her role as Luna Lovegood in the Harry Potter film franchise.
The wedding reception took place at Wilton’s Music Hall with a swing band.
The couple got engaged in August 2023 following an earlier informal proposal.

title: Kit Harington to replace Nicholas Hoult in HBO’s Harry Potter TV series
author: Nadia Khomami
content:
Kit Harington will replace Nicholas Hoult in HBO’s Harry Potter television series, after the Skins actor left the production because of scheduling conflicts.
Harington will play Gilderoy Lockhart, the vain and inept defence against the dark arts teacher, in the season based on Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, the second novel in JK Rowling’s series. The casting change was announced just two weeks after Hoult was confirmed for the role.
Hoult, who played Lex Luthor in the recent Superman film, was released from the Harry Potter production after its filming schedule conflicted with his other commitments.
Harington is best known for playing Jon Snow in Game of Thrones, as well as a more recent appearance in the BBC/HBO drama Industry.
The actor voiced Lockhart in Audible’s full-cast adaptation of The Chamber of Secrets, released in 2025. He said recently that he was a longstanding Harry Potter fan and described Lockhart as one of his favourite characters.
“I’m thrilled,” Harington told Collider. “I’ve said a million times, for anyone who cares, that I’m a huge Potter fan.
“I’ve got to be honest, he’s one of my favourite characters. So, to be offered to play him is a real dream. I think he’s going to be so fun. I got to play him in the audiobooks. That’s not the exact way I’ll play him in the show because it’s an audiobook, but I’ve had a taste of him and felt my way around him. He’s just a wonderful creation.”
Lockhart is a celebrity wizard and prolific author whose reputation is built on supposedly heroic exploits that, it emerges, were largely the work of other witches and wizards. He was previously played by Kenneth Branagh in the 2002 film adaptation.
The HBO series is intended to retell Rowling’s seven-book story over multiple seasons, with each season expected to be based on a different novel. The first season, Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone, is due to premiere on 25 December. Production on the second season is scheduled to begin this autumn.
The series stars Dominic McLaughlin as Harry, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley. John Lithgow plays Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer is Minerva McGonagall, Nick Frost plays Rubeus Hagrid and Paapa Essiedu plays Severus Snape.
Harington’s appointment is the latest change to the cast. Gracie Cochrane, who plays Ginny Weasley in the first season, is also leaving the series and will be replaced for its second season.
Hoult, along with other cast members, has faced some backlash for his decision to join the show from those opposed to Rowling’s views on sex and gender.
summary: Kit Harington has been cast as Gilderoy Lockhart in HBO's Harry Potter television series, replacing Nicholas Hoult due to scheduling conflicts. Harington, who previously voiced the character in a 2025 Audible adaptation, will appear in the second season based on Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets. The multi-season series adapts JK Rowling's books, with the first season premiering on December 25.
key_points: Kit Harington is replacing Nicholas Hoult as Gilderoy Lockhart for the second season of HBO's Harry Potter series.
Nicholas Hoult left the production due to scheduling conflicts with his other commitments.
Harington previously voiced Lockhart in an Audible full-cast adaptation released in 2025.
The first season of the HBO series is scheduled to premiere on December 25.
Gracie Cochrane is also leaving her role as Ginny Weasley and will be replaced for the second season.

title: Nicholas Hoult pulls out of Harry Potter series after trans backlash
author: Tom McArdle
content:
![Nicholas Hoult had been set to play Gilderoy Lockhart in the HBO series](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000430936251_17876516860010_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq1bM-xv9DsvcFg6dWh1HUcz4Sqm8f_Qqk9Ing3pOqdps.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Nicholas Hoult had been set to play Gilderoy Lockhart in the HBO series](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000430936251_17876516860010_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq1bM-xv9DsvcFg6dWh1HUcz4Sqm8f_Qqk9Ing3pOqdps.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Nicholas Hoult has pulled out of the new Harry Potter television series following a backlash from pro-trans fans.
The Skins actor, 36, had been set to play Gilderoy Lockhart in the HBO reboot of JK Rowling’s novels.
But Hoult, who was only cast in the upcoming second series earlier this month, has left two weeks after his role was announced.
He blamed scheduling issues, but the decision came after Hoult was criticised by pro-trans campaigners.
![Kenneth Branagh as Gilderoy Lockhart and Daniel Radcliffe in Harry Potter And The Chamber of Secrets in 2002](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499489764_17876516949101_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqmlTH6d1nWgN1IPYb78K207SZlaO_Mu_K8n4T04eaOmk.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The Golden Globe winner has a large LGBT fanbase after playing characters including Tony Stonem, a bisexual, in Skins and Kenny Potter in the 2009 film A Single Man.
Rowling is a prominent gender-critical and pro-women’s rights campaigner whom some campaigners have labelled as transphobic. She has always denied this.
As a result, many of the actors taking up roles in the new television series have faced criticism from her opponents, who believe the show should be boycotted.
LGBT online magazine Them said Hoult had “burned queer goodwill” by taking the role.
![Harry Potter is played by Dominic McLaughlin in the new series](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000432435888_17876517000450_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq3Z7i_2nUjuO-XXgVmfiyhF3PO22CeHK5NwuG70nO9dQ.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
A host of social media users criticised him, with one stating that he had had “so much good will until this point” with a black-and-white photo of Hoult with the years 1989-2026, seemingly making reference to the end of his allied status.
A fan account dedicated to Hoult wrote on X: “Pausing any posts on this account for the time being. Nicholas Hoult do better, so many of your fans are hurt.”
Another said: “Incredibly disappointed. Used to be one of my favourite actors but oh well.”
Kit Harington, the Game of Thrones star, has been announced as his replacement.
Rowling’s campaigning previously led to criticism from Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint, who made their names in the film adaptations of her books.
Ally Pankiw, one of the directors of the TV series Black Mirror, was the latest to comment publicly after claiming she had turned down being part of the new show over Rowling’s “transphobia”.
![Kit Harington has been announced as Hoult's replacement](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000198971152_17876518846680_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqBlCBoRe8MniIA2hNFAid6Lh24fySxJF1nCHEpNMVq7c.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Earlier this year, John Lithgow, who plays headmaster Albus Dumbledore in the new series, said it had been “a hard decision” to accept the role in light of the author’s gender-critical views, which he called inexplicable.
In September last year, Rowling addressed the falling out with Radcliffe, Watson and Grint for the first time.
The bestselling author said: “Like other people who’ve never experienced adult life un-cushioned by wealth and fame, Emma has so little experience of real life, she’s ignorant of how ignorant she is.
“I wasn’t a multimillionaire at 14. I lived in poverty while writing the book that made Emma famous. I therefore understand from my own life experience what the trashing of women’s rights, in which Emma has so enthusiastically participated, means to women and girls without her privileges.”
In March, a trans-owned independent bookshop in Leeds invited customers to deface Harry Potter books for 25p a page, with the funds raised put towards healthcare for transgender people.
One message addressed to Rowling read: “You’ve ruined yourself, ruined the name of feminism and ruined the precious childhood of thousands of women and girls.”
Filming for the second season of Harry Potter is expected to start this autumn, while the first season will come out on HBO and HBO Max on Christmas Day.
summary: Nicholas Hoult has withdrawn from his role as Gilderoy Lockhart in the upcoming HBO Harry Potter television series just two weeks after his casting was announced. Although he cited scheduling issues, the decision followed backlash and criticism from pro-trans campaigners and members of his LGBT fanbase. Kit Harington has been announced as Hoult's replacement for the series.
key_points: Nicholas Hoult pulled out of the HBO Harry Potter series following criticism from pro-trans campaigners.
Hoult had been cast as Gilderoy Lockhart for the second season just two weeks prior.
Kit Harington has been announced to replace Hoult in the role.
JK Rowling's gender-critical views have previously led to criticism and backlash from various actors and public figures connected to the franchise.

title: Ted Lasso actor opens up on battle with depression before popular Apple TV series
author: Lauren Del Fabbro
content:
Brett Goldstein has revealed that keeping a gratitude journal transformed his mindset after experiencing depression prior to the success of Ted Lasso.
The 46-year-old British actor and comedian plays Roy Kent, a retired footballer turned assistant coach, in the Apple TV comedy Ted Lasso, which stars Jason Sudeikis as a Midwestern American football coach hired to manage fictional side AFC Richmond despite having no experience in the sport.
Upon its 2020 debut, the show became an immediate success and set a record for the highest number of Emmy nominations received by a first-season comedy, with Goldstein winning the award for outstanding supporting actor in a comedy in both 2021 and 2022.
Before the series catapulted him to fame, Goldstein struggled with his mental health. His therapist advised him to start a gratitude journal, tasking him with noting down at least 10 positive moments every day.
![Brett Goldstein, 46, plays Roy Kent in the hit show Ted Lasso](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/08/25/01/01KT7CE2YGEX0KDREM8YKWPQGR.jpg)
Speaking to Men’s Health UK, he said: "I was depressed.
"Every day she (the therapist) made me write a list of 10 things that happened that day that I was grateful for.
"In the beginning, when you’re so, so depressed, it’s like, ‘Nothing’. But you have to put 10 in. ‘The sun was up.’ That’s one. You start so small. But by day 30 of doing that, you’ve started training your brain to look for the positive, and I could write a list of 100 things. I’m the luckiest guy in the world! Everything’s f****** amazing!’"
A few weeks into the practice, Goldstein noticed a clear shift in how he viewed the world, noting that while he still experiences difficult periods, learning to value smaller moments continues to support him.
He said: "It really had changed me, built new synapses, whatever it is. You can look for the good. It’s a f****** skill – or, something you have to work at.
"I don’t always achieve it. I still have darker days. But gratitude helps."
Reflecting on expectations around masculinity, Goldstein explained that while his family did not explicitly discourage showing feelings, he still felt broader social pressures to suppress his emotions.
He said: "I definitely grew up with the feelings of, ‘Men aren’t supposed to show emotions.’ But then I got older, and my experience with women was whenever I was accidentally vulnerable it went very well.
"I was like, ‘Oh, I guess I’ve been learning the wrong lessons.’"
He said something similar was also true of men’s relationship with body image.
"My trainer in New York, he was a professional bodybuilder and there are pictures of him on the wall in amazing shape. He said, ‘Men love it. Women hate it.’
"There are all these things where I think most people don’t know what they’re doing, they have been behaving how they think they’re meant to behave."
Beside his role in Ted Lasso, Goldstein has appeared in the television series Shrinking, starred in the 2024 film All Of You, and features in the romantic comedy Office Romance alongside pop star Jennifer Lopez.
The full interview with Brett Goldstein appears in the September issue of Men’s Health UK, which is on sale now.
summary: Actor Brett Goldstein revealed that maintaining a gratitude journal helped transform his mindset after battling depression before finding fame in the Apple TV series Ted Lasso. Advised by his therapist to write down ten positive moments daily, Goldstein trained his brain to notice the good, significantly shifting his perspective. He also discussed societal pressures regarding masculinity and body image, noting that vulnerability has ultimately served him well.
key_points: Brett Goldstein struggled with depression prior to achieving success and recognition in Ted Lasso.
His therapist instructed him to write down 10 things he was grateful for every day.
The daily journaling practice helped retrain his brain to focus on positive moments.
Goldstein reflected on social pressures regarding masculinity and how learning to be vulnerable changed his life.
He plays Roy Kent in Ted Lasso and has won two Emmy Awards for the role.

title: Australia’s music charts ban AI-made songs amid backlash over Madonna cover
author: John Power
content:
![AI](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/AI-1787623060.jpeg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Australia’s official music charts have banned tracks mostly created by artificial intelligence (AI) following a backlash over a cover of Madonna’s “Like a Prayer” that relied heavily on the burgeoning technology.
“Wholly AI-generated” music will be excluded from the charts under the changes, while tracks that use AI in a “supporting role” will still be eligible, the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) said on Tuesday.

- list 4 of 4Man killed in world’s largest annual bullfighting event in Mexico
AI-generated music will also not be considered for recognition at the annual ARIA Music Awards under the new rules, which are set to take effect on Friday.
ARIA said it would rely on a labelling system introduced by music industry groups last month to distinguish AI-generated tracks from those that use AI to complement human creativity.
Under the labelling rules announced by a coalition of organisations including the Recording Industry Association of America, tracks may be labelled “AI-Generated” or “AI-Assisted” depending on the level of human involvement in the writing and recording process.
Tracks are classed as “AI-Generated” if AI was used to create the “entirety or the primary portion of the creative elements of the recording” and “AI-Assisted” if the technology was used only for “some expressive elements”.
ARIA CEO Annabelle Herd said while the music charts should evolve to reflect the legitimate use of AI, they should not recognise music generated “wholesale” by technology that relies on other artists’ work.
“These changes reflect our intent to remain dynamic and promote the human nature of artistry in what is – to say the least – a rapidly developing space,” Herd said in a statement.
ARIA, whose members include major music labels such as Sony Music Entertainment Australia and Universal Music Australia, publishes more than two dozen weekly music charts in Australia, including the top 50 singles and top 50 albums.
![Madonna performs during a surprise concert in Times Square, in New York, US, on June 4, 2026](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/madonna-1787634147.jpeg?w=770&resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
The industry association’s decision comes after a Brisbane-based DJ’s chart-topping cover of Madonna’s 1989 hit Like a Prayer attracted a backlash over its use of AI-generated vocals and drums.
Josh Fawaz last month belatedly acknowledged using AI on the track after music fans and producers raised suspicions that it was not produced by a human.
The cover has racked up more than 48.5 million listens on music streaming platform Spotify and currently ranks number one on the ARIA Top 20 Australian Dance Singles Chart.
Fawaz, who has defended the use of AI as a “tool” in his music, described ARIA’s new rules as a “great move”.
“I understand that AI in music isn’t for everyone and that’s fine. Good to see Aussie artists killing it globally!!” Fawaz wrote in a social media post responding to the announcement.
Oliver Bown, an associate professor at the University of New South Wales who researches the relationship between technology and art, said the impact of AI on creative industries such as music demands urgent attention.
“Many large commercial AI music generation companies have assumed they can scrape training data without permission, and so are potentially predatory on artists,” Bown told Al Jazeera.
“I believe people can do great artistic work using AI respectfully, but there is also a predatory phenomenon whereby you can just go fishing for plays and profits,” he added.
“Many organisations have developed rules about AI use and an increasing number see the need to ban full-AI works. I think this is the right thing to do.”
Ivan Zavada, a senior lecturer in composition and music technology at the University of Sydney, said the changes have been widely viewed as a “necessary step” to protect “genuine human musical creativity and performance”.
“More work needs to be done on the legal and intellectual property fronts to enable more trust and clarity in these tools,” Zavada told Al Jazeera.
“AI will be an essential part of standard music production in the very near future. We are living a very exciting yet concerning transition period in the digital and electronic arts.”
summary: Australia's official music charts have banned wholly AI-generated tracks following backlash over a Brisbane DJ's popular AI-assisted cover of Madonna's "Like a Prayer." Under new rules set by the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA), music created primarily by artificial intelligence will be excluded from the charts and the annual ARIA Music Awards. Tracks that use AI in a supporting or complementary role will still remain eligible.
key_points: Australia's official music charts and ARIA Music Awards are banning wholly AI-generated music starting Friday.
Tracks that use AI in a supporting role, known as "AI-Assisted," will still be eligible for the charts.
The policy change follows a backlash over a chart-topping AI-assisted cover of Madonna's "Like a Prayer" by Brisbane-based DJ Josh Fawaz.
ARIA will use a newly introduced labelling system to distinguish between tracks created primarily by AI and those where AI merely complements human creativity.

title: James Blunt shares article denying Hayden Panettiere rumours
author: Iona Cleave
content:
![Since Panettiere's death, theories began circulating that Blunt was the British singer she wrote about in her memoir](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000436141623_17876068563600_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Since Panettiere's death, theories began circulating that Blunt was the British singer she wrote about in her memoir](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000436141623_17876068563600_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
James Blunt shared an article denying that American actress Hayden Panettiere was brought to his bed when she was 18.
Panettiere, a former child actress known for her roles in Nashville and Heroes, died on Aug 16 aged 36 in a suspected overdose. Her official cause of death has not yet been revealed.
In her May 2026 autobiography This Is Me: A Reckoning, Panettiere recounted an incident in which she said an unnamed woman asked her to get in bed with an “undressed” and “very famous” British singer in his 30s on a yacht in France.
She wrote that she was 18 at the time and the incident led to her hiding on the boat.
Since her death, theories began circulating that Blunt was the unidentified British singer-songwriter she wrote about in her memoir. Online sleuths pointed to a picture of the pair together in 2009.
![James Blunt, Justin Long, Hayden Panettiere and Diana Jenkins at a party during Cannes Film Festival in 2009](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499466522_17876079978580_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq-x7cCC-ZG6ze-hWeTskdmHdR78eTBj0hwdfFRfV9oOU.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Pushing back on the growing speculation that Panettiere was referring to him, Blunt shared an article with his two million followers on X denying the rumours.
Dean Piper, a British journalist, wrote in the piece: “Here lies the problem with the Wild West of internet chatter. Facts don’t matter. Legalities don’t matter. People are saying whatever they like and getting away with it and that is wrong.”
Mr Piper, who reported on Panettiere and Blunt spending time together at Cannes in 2009, said the timeline of the internet theory does not make sense. He pointed out that Panettiere was 19, not 18, in Cannes.
“Guys, it only takes the smallest of AI searches to find out that in May 2009, when the pictures of Blunt and Panettiere were taken, she was 19, almost 20. So, if the incident happened when she was 18, Blunt’s not your guy to start with,” he says.
Elsewhere in her memoir, Panettiere spoke about the perils of early fame, postpartum depression, addiction and recovery, trauma, domestic abuse, and the loss of her brother.
According to a police report obtained by NBC, a “bag of medication” was found at the apartment where Panettiere died.
She was with her on-and-off-again boyfriend Brian Hickerson in an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina, at the time of her death.
Mr Hickerson was arrested several times for domestic abuse during the pair’s on-off relationship, which lasted between 2018 and 2022.
The local police department said the preliminary investigation did not “indicate any signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances”.
Her mother, Lesley Vogel, told ABC News on Monday that she wanted her daughter “to be remembered for the talented, you know, beautiful, outgoing, intelligent woman she really was”.
Blunt is set to be a contestant on the next season of Celebrity Traitors, the highly watched spin-off of the British reality TV show Traitors, expected to air in the autumn.
summary: James Blunt shared an article on X denying online speculation that he was the unnamed British singer mentioned in Hayden Panettiere's memoir. Theories had circulated following Panettiere's death at age 36, connecting Blunt to an incident she described involving an 18-year-old on a yacht. However, the shared article and journalist Dean Piper pointed out that the timeline does not align because Panettiere was 19 when she was photographed with Blunt in Cannes in 2009.
key_points: James Blunt pushed back against internet rumors by sharing an article denying he was the singer described in Hayden Panettiere's memoir.
Panettiere passed away on August 16 at the age of 36 in a suspected overdose, with her official cause of death still unrevealed.
In her 2026 autobiography, Panettiere wrote about an incident at age 18 involving an unnamed, famous British singer on a French yacht.
Online speculation linked Blunt to the memoir based on 2009 photographs, but journalists noted the timeline fails because Panettiere was 19 at the time of those photos.

title: Ted Lasso actor reveals daily habit that helped with depression
author: Lauren Del Fabbro
content:
Ted Lasso actor reveals daily habit that helped with depression
- Ted Lasso star Brett Goldstein has revealed that keeping a gratitude journal helped transform his mindset after experiencing depression before achieving mainstream fame.
- The 46-year-old actor was advised by his therapist to record 10 positive moments daily, a practice he says trained his brain to look for the good in life.
- Goldstein, who won back-to-back Emmy awards in 2021 and 2022 for playing Roy Kent in the Apple TV comedy, acknowledged that he still works to maintain a positive outlook on darker days.
- In an interview with Men's Health UK, he also discussed overcoming societal pressures around masculinity and learning the value of emotional vulnerability.
- Outside of his breakthrough role, Goldstein has appeared in the series Shrinking, the film All Of You, and the romantic comedy Office Romance.
summary: Actor Brett Goldstein revealed that keeping a gratitude journal significantly helped him manage depression before achieving mainstream fame. Advised by his therapist to record ten positive moments daily, the practice trained his brain to focus on the good in life. In a recent interview, he also discussed overcoming societal pressures related to masculinity and the importance of emotional vulnerability.
key_points: Brett Goldstein used a gratitude journal to help transform his mindset after experiencing depression.
His therapist recommended recording 10 positive moments daily to train his brain to find the good in life.
Goldstein discussed overcoming societal pressures regarding masculinity and embracing emotional vulnerability.
The Emmy-winning actor is known for his role as Roy Kent in Ted Lasso.

title: Freddie Mercury’s ‘splendid things’ to go on display at V&A
author: Nadia Khomami
content:
Eight famous costumes worn by Freddie Mercury, including the outfit featured on the cover of Queen’s debut album and the catsuit from the video for Bohemian Rhapsody, are to go on display at the V&A in London this autumn to mark what would have been the singer’s 80th birthday.
Freddie Mercury | Splendid Things, a free trail developed with Mercury’s former fiancee and close friend Mary Austin, will run from 24 October 2026 to 17 January 2027. Austin is lending seven of the looks, which span Mercury’s career from the 1970s to his final years.
Among them is a monochrome ensemble worn for an early Queen gig at Imperial College and pictured on the cover of the band’s eponymous debut album. Also on display will be the “Mercury Wing” catsuit, designed by Wendy de Smet and worn during the A Night at the Opera tour in 1975-76, as well as in the groundbreaking Bohemian Rhapsody video.
Mercury’s crown and cloak, designed by Diana Moseley and worn during Queen’s 1986 Magic Tour, will also feature. He wore the outfit for the band’s final live performance at Knebworth that year. The display will also include a costume from the Made in Heaven music video, as well as accessories and items from his personal wardrobe.
![Head and shoulders shot of Mercury clasping ornate crown on his head with red-and-white ermine-style cloak](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/f2cbb5d16de4d03ccc777892916ca5fc8b1810a4/0_0_714_751/master/714.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The trail takes its name from a remark Mercury made in 1978: “I like to be surrounded by splendid things. I want to lead a Victorian life surrounded by exquisite clutter.”
Austin first met Mercury when she was 19 and he was 24, while they were both working around Kensington’s Biba fashion scene. Mercury, born as Farrokh Bulsara on 5 September 1946 in Zanzibar, was selling his artwork and vintage clothes from a stall in Kensington Market. They became engaged on Christmas Day 1973, the year Queen released their debut album.
Their relationship ended in the mid-1970s, but they remained close for the rest of Mercury’s life. When he died in 1991, he left Austin his Kensington home, Garden Lodge, and his possessions.
Austin has described Mercury’s clothes as central to the image he created as a performer. “The clothes were part of that exploration,” she said in A Life in Lyrics, due to be published in September. “Freddie understood early on that he wasn’t just wearing clothes; he was providing an image to match the scale of the space and the vastness of the crowd.”
![Head and shoulders shot of Mercury in black outfit with red sash](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/955302ff83c452d9c1142731024e57745463e214/0_67_3300_3377/master/3300.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Austin said the clothes and costumes to be displayed at the V&A “tell a hugely important part” of Mercury’s story both on and off the stage: “Never mere accoutrements, his costumes and clothes were essential to his performances, creative vision, and wider self-expression, carefully designed to create a lasting visual and emotional impact that has reached across the generations and still reverberates today.”
The installations have been designed by Tom Piper, whose work includes productions for the Royal Shakespeare Company, the Tower of London poppies and the V&A’s Alice: Curiouser and Curiouser and Taylor Swift | Songbook Trail.
Each of the trail’s six stops will be staged differently, using sets, sound and lighting to evoke moments from Mercury’s career.
Kate Bailey, the V&A’s senior curator of theatre and performance, said the display would explore Mercury’s “love of ‘splendid things’” and his interest in art, design and fashion.
summary: Eight famous costumes and personal wardrobe items worn by Freddie Mercury will go on display at the V&A in London this autumn to mark what would have been his 80th birthday. Developed with Mercury's former fiancée and close friend Mary Austin, the free trail titled "Freddie Mercury | Splendid Things" will run from October 24, 2026, to January 17, 2027. The exhibition features iconic looks spanning his career, including the catsuit from the "Bohemian Rhapsody" video and the crown and cloak from his final live performance in 1986.
key_points: The V&A exhibition will run from 24 October 2026 to 17 January 2027 to mark what would have been Freddie Mercury's 80th birthday.
Mary Austin is lending seven of the eight featured looks, spanning Mercury's career from the 1970s to his final years.
Featured items include the "Mercury Wing" catsuit from the "Bohemian Rhapsody" video and the crown and cloak worn during the 1986 Magic Tour.
The free trail will feature six stops designed by Tom Piper, utilizing sets, sound, and lighting to evoke moments from Mercury's career.

title: Guardian-produced Gaza documentary from Oscar-winning Israeli directors of No Other Land to screen at Venice film festival
author: Andrew Pulver
content:
A new documentary about Israel’s bombing campaign in Gaza, directed by Oscar-winning directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, is to receive its world premiere at the Venice film festival.
The film, called NAZA, has been produced with Jim Wilson and executive produced by Jonathan Glazer, the team behind The Zone of Interest, and is the only documentary that will compete this year for Venice’s prestigious Golden Lion.
Abraham and Szor are the two Israeli directors of the four behind No Other Land, which won the Oscar for best documentary in 2025.
Announcing the news, the film-makers said: “Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.”
The Guardian added in a statement that NAZA is an Israeli military acronym used euphemistically by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians that it expects will be killed in an airstrike.
The documentary builds on original investigative reporting between 2023 and 2025 by Israeli-Palestinian publication +972, Hebrew-language outlet Local Call and the Guardian.
No Other Land, which was directed by Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal alongside Abraham and Szor, was described as a “sombre, sobering work” by the Guardian’s chief film critic Peter Bradshaw.
Shortly after No Other Land’s Oscar win, Ballal was attacked by Israeli settlers and briefly arrested, following which the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences apologised after failing to name Ballal or the film in a statement of support.
summary: A new Guardian-produced documentary titled NAZA, directed by Oscar-winning Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, is set to premiere at the Venice film festival. The film is the sole documentary competing for the festival's Golden Lion award this year. It details the systems behind Israel's military campaign in Gaza, drawing on investigative reporting conducted between 2023 and 2025.
key_points: The documentary NAZA will have its world premiere at the Venice film festival.
It is directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, who co-directed the Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land.
The film is the only documentary competing for Venice's Golden Lion this year.
NAZA was produced by the Guardian and Jim Wilson, with Jonathan Glazer serving as executive producer.
The film builds on investigative reporting by the Guardian, +972, and Local Call.

title: Rivals star Emily Atack shares photos from "absolutely perfect" wedding ceremony to long-term partner
author: Joe Anderton
content:
Rivals and The Inbetweeners star Emily Atack tied the knot to her partner Alistair Garner in a stunning wedding ceremony yesterday, and teased that there's another one to come!
The actor and the scientist have been dating for the last few years, although they know each other from childhood. As Atack told The Guardian previously, he is her "aunt's husband's son by a previous marriage" and found the rumours that she was 'dating her cousin' "really hurtful".
It was all smiles yesterday as she wore a white plunge gown with lace-fluted sleeves and a similar floral-looking pattern on the skirt, while he wore a black suit paired with white socks and tan shoes.
Atack shared some photos of them walking out of the venue surrounded by loved ones and posing in front of an old-fashioned car in a shady woodland area.
"Yesterday we officially got married among close family and friends. It was absolutely perfect", she wrote in the caption, before teasing that they're going to have yet another celebration very soon.
"I can't believe we get to do all that again in a few weeks' time. Christ, we have fun, don't we."
On her Instagram Stories, Atack shared more photos from the ceremony as well as a post from her makeup artist cousin Lydia Barnes, who noted that Atack did do her own bronzer for the big day.
Atack also shared a post from bridalwear designer Avenue by Josephine Scott, which explained that she approached wedding boutique Evelie with "a clear vision, an elegant gown with a contemporary edge and something unexpected".
The designer's post also included a video of the "striking" keyhole back that we didn't get to see in Atack's own post.
Stacey Dooley, Giovanna Fletcher, Ruth Langsford, Amanda Holden, Christine Lampard, Vicky Pattison, Sophie Habboo, and Denise Welch were just some of the many celebrities to comment on the posts.
In other Emily Atack news, it was recently reported that the bosses behind The Inebetweeners revival are really keen to get her to sign up and play her breakout role Charlotte Hinchcliffe again.
