title: Dutch to boycott Eurovision again after organisers refuse to expel Israel
author: James Crisp
content:
![Joost Klein of Netherlands arrives on stage for the introducing of the artists at the dress rehearsal for the final at the Eurovision Song Contest in Malmo, Sweden, Friday, May 10, 2024](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000377152510_17875836661810_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqwsT-9OTSBDUotCuRrPr5Io28T2hbZHXZ22h8Por1ONw.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Joost Klein of Netherlands arrives on stage for the introducing of the artists at the dress rehearsal for the final at the Eurovision Song Contest in Malmo, Sweden, Friday, May 10, 2024](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000377152510_17875836661810_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqwsT-9OTSBDUotCuRrPr5Io28T2hbZHXZ22h8Por1ONw.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
The Netherlands is poised to boycott the Eurovision Song Contest for the second year in a row because of Israel’s war in Gaza.
Avrotros, the public broadcaster, said the event could “no longer be considered neutral” because of the divisions among countries over Israel taking part in the competition.
It said that new rules designed to guarantee the contest’s political neutrality were not sufficient, meaning it had to make the “painful” decision to continue its boycott.
Earlier this month, organisers of the contest announced that they would exclude any country involved in an armed conflict from hosting the world’s biggest live televised music event.
![Taco Zimmerman, director-general of Avrotros](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000377207388_17875838810550_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqhz8HEu5oiqyCKtha3acuUrNgKGENc6o7rVeLApzjLc8.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
“It is undeniable that international conflicts are increasingly affecting the Contest, undermining its neutral character. The Eurovision Song Contest has therefore become a platform for division,” said Taco Zimmerman, the director-general of Avrotros.
“The recently announced changes... do not provide sufficient confidence that the independent and neutral character of the Eurovision Song Contest has been restored.”
He added: “As a public broadcaster, we remain committed to our values. They guide us in everything we do, even when that means stepping away from an event that is very close to our hearts.”
Avrotros has returned responsibility for the Dutch entry to the Nederlandse Publieke Omroep (NPO), which is the governing body of public broadcasting in the Netherlands. It will make a final decision on how to proceed.
The Dutch broadcaster is the first to confirm it won’t be involved in the 2027 iteration of the competition in Bulgaria, which is organised by the European Broadcasting Union (EBU).
The Netherlands was one of five countries, including Spain, Ireland, Slovenia and Iceland, to boycott this year’s 70th anniversary contest in Vienna.
The EBU was set to hold a divisive vote among public broadcasters on whether to kick out Israel’s KAN channel.
Hosts Austria and Germany both said they would leave the competition if Israel was excluded, amid surging anti-Semitism in Europe after the Oct 7 terror attacks and accusations of war crimes in Gaza.
The vote was postponed after the October ceasefire and ultimately was not held.
In December, most broadcasters agreed instead to toughen rules on political neutrality and government meddling in phone voting, which led to the boycott.
![Israel's Yuval Raphael celebrates coming second in Eurovision with an Israeli flag](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000451800889_17875849315480_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqI4i1a-7tqjMxGle8m6q3UP4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Israel finished second in both 2025 and 2026. There were accusations of vote-rigging after Israel’s Yuval Raphael was unexpectedly catapulted into second place from 14th by the televote in 2025.
The 2026 competition was watched by 131 million viewers, down 35 million on the year before after the five-country boycott. Spain, Ireland and Slovenia refused to broadcast the show at all.
Next year’s event will take place on May 15 in the Black Sea city of Burgas.
It will be the first time Bulgaria will host the contest after its singer Dara triumphed in Vienna with catchy floor-filler Bangaranga.
In 2022, Eurovision organisers set a precedent for banning warring countries from participating when it kicked Russia out of the contest when Vladimir Putin launched the invasion of Ukraine.
It has not been allowed to return since, and has instead held its own equivalent competition – the Intervision Song Contest – featuring countries including Belarus, China and Saudi Arabia.
The Dutch took part in the first Eurovision Song Contest in 1956, and have won it five times.
Martin Green, the director of the Eurovision Song Contest, said the organisation regretted but respected the decision.
He said organisers would investigate whether another Dutch broadcaster might be willing to participate in the contest.
summary: The Netherlands is set to boycott the Eurovision Song Contest for a second consecutive year because organisers refused to expel Israel over the war in Gaza. Dutch broadcaster Avrotros stated that the event can no longer be considered neutral and that new rules implemented by the European Broadcasting Union are insufficient. The Netherlands is the first country to confirm its absence from the 2027 contest in Bulgaria.
key_points: The Dutch public broadcaster Avrotros announced it will continue its Eurovision boycott due to Israel's participation.
Organisers updated political neutrality rules instead of holding a vote to expel Israel's KAN channel, which Avrotros deemed insufficient.
The Netherlands joins previous boycotters like Spain, Ireland, and Slovenia in opposing the contest's handling of the conflict.
The 2027 Eurovision Song Contest is scheduled to take place in Burgas, Bulgaria, on May 15.

title: Has Meghan Markle been dropped from her acting comeback?
author: David Mouriquand
content:
There has been speculation that Meghan Markle was set to make her return to acting following her return to the UK. A rumoured role in Guy Ritchie’s show The Gentlemen was on the table... and has now apparently been withdrawn “after intense backlash in the UK”...
Ever since last week's news that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle were planning to move back to the UK for an “extended period” following six years of living in California, the rumour mill has been working overtime.
It’s hardly surprising considering how divisive Markle is as a public figure and how the British press has piled on repeatedly when it comes to criticising every move she makes.
Alongside the headline-grabbing news that the couple are returning to the UK after a very public and controversial break with the British royal family, there have been contradictory reports that Markle would be returning to acting.
The main speculation has been that Markle was being considered to join Guy Ritchie’s Netflix series The Gentlemen upon her return to England. Australian news outlet News.com.au reported that she had been “offered a role in an upcoming project based in the UK”. Variety subsequently reported that this role would be in the planned third season of the series spin-off of Ritchie’s 2019 movie of the same name.
The project would make sense, as Markle and Prince Harry’s Archewell Productions already has a working relationship with Netflix – with the companies having produced Markle’s critically savaged lifestyle show With Love, Meghan, as well as poorly received projects like Harry & Meghan, Polo, and the docuseries Heart of Invictus.
However, it now seems that the offer to star in The Gentlemen has been withdrawn – if it even existed in the first place.
Tina Brown, the former editor-in-chief of Vanity Fair and the New Yorker, wrote this weekend: “I learned this morning that the casting of Meghan Markle in season 3 of Guy Ritchie’s Netflix series The Gentlemen has been withdrawn. The backlash in the UK was so intense, it became untenable to go forward.”
It is unclear whether the story was originally planted to generate publicity or if it was fake to begin with. Whatever the case may be, if Markle was planning to make an acting comeback, it won’t be smooth sailing.
Primarily known for her role as Rachel Zane in the legal drama Suits, Markle stepped back from the small screen in 2017 before she married Prince Harry.
Her other small screen appearances include CSI: NY, 90210, Fringe and Castle. Her film roles have included small parts in Horrible Bosses (2011), Dysfunctional Friends (2012) and Anti-Social (2015). She also led two Hallmark movies: When Sparks Fly (2014) and Dater’s Handbook (2016).
She recently filmed a cameo playing herself in the Amazon comedy Close Personal Friends alongside Brie Larson, Lily Collins and Jack Quaid. A release date has yet to be announced.
Read more
![Prince Harry and Meghan wave from their carriage after their wedding at Windsor Castle on 19 May 2018. (Paul Ellis/Pool Photo via AP)](https://images.euronews.com/articles/stories/09/88/19/67/480x270_cmsv2_9c3a1168-47ca-5d48-b05b-8100bc7d9d0e-9881967.jpg) 
![Prince Harry  and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, in 2022.](https://images.euronews.com/articles/stories/09/41/65/68/480x270_cmsv2_9c3b44c3-2cd1-521e-9b7d-81192abc2d15-9416568.jpg) 
![Meghan Markle’s new brand logo sparks controversy over alleged copycat design](https://images.euronews.com/articles/stories/09/07/11/88/480x270_cmsv2_33faea09-10a1-5f95-bf41-69cc07cab820-9071188.jpg)
summary: Rumours suggested that Meghan Markle was offered a role in the third season of Guy Ritchie's Netflix series "The Gentlemen" following news of her and Prince Harry's potential return to the UK. However, former magazine editor Tina Brown reported that the casting offer has reportedly been withdrawn due to intense backlash in the UK. It remains unclear whether the initial casting report was a publicity plant or entirely fabricated.
key_points: Meghan Markle was reportedly considered for a role in season three of Guy Ritchie's Netflix series "The Gentlemen".
Tina Brown stated that the casting offer was withdrawn due to intense backlash in the UK.
Markle and Prince Harry's production company, Archewell Productions, already has an existing working relationship with Netflix.
Markle stepped away from her acting career in 2017 before marrying Prince Harry.

title: Kit Harington joins HBO's Harry Potter series as Gilderoy Lockhart
author: Nardine Saad
content:
![Kit Harrington appears on the red carpet for a premier](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/10a5/live/bee5d940-9ffe-11f1-8a82-5d6af15250d2.jpg)
- Published
Kit Harington has been tapped to join the highly anticipated Harry Potter TV series as the wizarding world's celebrity-turned-Hogwarts instructor Gilderoy Lockhart, HBO confirmed to the BBC.
Harington is replacing actor Nicholas Hoult who could not film season two of the series due to a scheduling conflict.
Best known for playing Jon Snow for eight seasons in the award-winning series Game of Thrones, Harington also appears in the BBC and HBO financial drama Industry. The casting marks the English actor's third collaboration with the American network and streamer.
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone is due to premiere on Christmas this year on HBO Max.
Season two will adapt the second book in the series by JK Rowling, The Chamber of Secrets, which chronicle's Potter's second year at the magical school.
"Before we begin year two at Hogwarts, there has been a slight change due to schedule: Kit Harington will be stepping into the role of Gilderoy Lockhart," a story post reads on the official Harry Potter Instagram account.
The new series adaptation of the best-selling books stars newcomer Dominic McLaughlin as the boy wizard, Alastair Stout as his best friend Ron Weasley and Arabella Stanton as the young witch Hermione Granger.
Oscar-nominated actor Jon Lithgow has been cast as Hogwarts headmaster Albus Dumbledore and Nick Frost as gamekeeper Rubeus Hagrid.
![Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter and Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger walk the halls of Hogwarts in their wizarding robes in HBO Max's new Harry Potter series.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/6ae5/live/2caacc20-9ff9-11f1-be19-71b839ccdc73.jpg)
The new series stars Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter and Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger.
![Kit Harrington seen smiling on the red carpet in a blue blazer](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/01db/live/a0f9c9b0-9ff3-11f1-b150-d3e6f0a6b415.jpg)
Kit Harington's casting marks his third role in a HBO series after Game of Thrones and the financial drama The Industry.
Emmy-award winning Harington, a lifelong fan of the books, already has some familiarity with his new role: The actor voiced Lockhart in Audible's star-studded Harry Potter: The Full-Cast Audio Editions last year.
The show could reunite him with director and producer Mark Mylod, who worked on Game of Thrones and is directing some Harry Potter episodes. Mylod is an executive producer on the new series along with author JK Rowling.
Lockhart was portrayed in the Warner Bros Harry Potter films by Kenneth Branagh, and is a key character in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, the second book in Rowling's best-selling franchise.
The vain wizard who authored several books on his purported encounters with dark creatures serves as Hogwarts' latest professor for the defence against the dark arts and fancies himself a mentor to Harry in his second year.
Hoult, known for his roles in X-Men, Superman and Mad Max: Fury Road, was announced for the role earlier this month. But HBO reportedly had to let the Superman actor out of his deal due to his commitments to projects that conflicted with a change in the series' production schedule, according to Deadline, which first reported Harington's casting. HBO confirmed the reporting to the BBC.
Representatives for Harington and Hoult did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The HBO series is expected to take 10 years to complete, as producers plan multiple seasons covering each of Rowling's seven books, which the eight blockbuster films were originally based on.
summary: Kit Harington has been cast as Gilderoy Lockhart in HBO's upcoming Harry Potter television series, replacing Nicholas Hoult due to scheduling conflicts. This marks Harington's third collaboration with HBO, following his work on Game of Thrones and Industry. Season two of the series will adapt The Chamber of Secrets, featuring Harington alongside a cast that includes Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter.
key_points: Kit Harington is joining HBO's Harry Potter series as Hogwarts instructor Gilderoy Lockhart.
Harington replaces Nicholas Hoult, who left the role due to a scheduling conflict.
The casting is Harington's third project with HBO, following Game of Thrones and Industry.
Season two of the series will adapt the second book, The Chamber of Secrets.
The new series stars Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, and Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger.

title: Charity? Acting? The Cotswolds? What will Harry and Meghan's UK life look like?
author: Daniela Relph; Daniel Wittenberg
content:
![Meghan holds onto Harry's arm as they wave at crowds while they walk from a car. Both are wearing brown. They are smiling.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/4648/live/54b5a5b0-9fdf-11f1-9c90-a93a719154c7.jpg)
Harry and Meghan's arrival back in Britain is imminent (the couple are seen here on their recent Australia tour)
- Published
Within the next few days, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex and their two children will have departed California and become residents of the UK.
Since news broke of the move, there has been some confusion as to what British life for Harry and Meghan will look like - but a picture is emerging of the family's priorities.
Over the weekend, there was a deluge of stories about Meghan's return to acting with speculation she would have a role in the next series of The Gentlemen on Netflix, created by British director Guy Ritchie.
Talks are still said to be in the early stages and we understand filming for the third series of the show is imminent - but Netflix has made no comment on who will star, leaving the way open for a former working member of the royal family with an acting background to be cast.
The comedy is about a duke turned drug baron and is mostly filmed in the Cotswolds.
What is clear is that a return to acting more broadly is very much on the agenda for Meghan. It would be financially lucrative for the family in a world of expensive homes, school fees and international travel.
'I miss my crew'
Speaking in June last year to British businesswoman and podcaster Emma Grede, Meghan talked about her Netflix lifestyle series With Love, Meghan, and hinted at a return to acting when asked if she missed that side to her life.
"Sometimes," Meghan replied. "Being back on set with With Love, Meghan was great because I realised how much I miss my crew. I love being around a crew."
But Variety's chief correspondent Marlow Stern says when it comes to deliberations over a potential acting role for Meghan, "a lot of it has to do with scheduling, to be honest".
"They're maybe also negotiating the size of the role and how many days she'll shoot, and also compensation for it. Both sides often play the media to try and push things along, and we could be seeing that."
For Harry, the focus once back in the UK will be on the charity work and patronages he has kept hold of while living thousands of miles away.
He has now completed his final charity engagements in the US before flying back to the UK in the coming days.
In Washington DC, he met military veterans and their families and visited America's main hospital for injured servicemen and women, Walter Reed National Military Medical Centre.
At Arlington National Cemetery, he visited the final resting place of many service personal killed in Iraq and Afghanistan wars where he himself served on two operational tours.
At the grave of Sergeant Michael Verardo, who died last year from complications related to injuries sustained in Afghanistan in 2010, he met Verardo's widow Sarah - who now supports other military families - and their nine-year-old daughter, Elizabeth.
![Prince Harry stands in a suit with military medals next to a mother who has one arm around her young daughter. They are standing on a green graveyard honouring military personnel with white gravestones.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/03bd/live/5bb2c4e0-9fdc-11f1-9c90-a93a719154c7.jpg)
Prince Harry met widow Sarah and her daughter Elizabeth, 9, at Arlington National Cemetery
"All my daughter knows about princes or princesses is probably contained to a movie... she whispered to me and said, 'Where is his crown? Did he leave it in the car?'" Sarah said.
"She was very dazzled by the ability to meet him and it made it made us find bits of sparkle for her at a young age in a very hard experience - and that means a lot to me personally."
It is a reminder of the impact Prince Harry is able to make and what he will hope to bring to an increased amount of public work in the UK.
Plans for a number of charity engagements in September in Britain were already in place.
He will be at the WellChild Awards in London towards the end of the month, continuing his support for the event which honours the bravery of seriously ill children.
There will inevitably be an emphasis on the Invictus Games for wounded service personnel which will be held in Birmingham next July.
In an ideal world, the King, as head of the Armed Forces, would officially open the Games - putting father and son together in public for the first time in several years.
That remains an aspiration from Invictus organisers rather than any definitive plan.
Based in the Cotswolds, settling into school
![Beige coloured shops line a picturesque high street in the Cotswolds.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/0f66/live/d10e9a60-9fdd-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
The couple are thought to have chosen the Cotswolds as their home (file image)
It's thought the family will base themselves in the Cotswolds. Harry and Meghan previously rented a property there in 2018 and are known to have friends in the area.
Reports that the couple have turned to former Spice Girl Geri Horner and her husband Christian Horner for advice on life in the area have been rejected by Harry and Meghan's official spokesperson.
"Harry and Meghan are great fans of Geri and Christianâ¦ the Horners are not advising them on their return, nor have they been asked to do so."
The couple will be back in the UK about a week before the autumn school term begins for their two children, seven-year-old Archie and five-year-old Lilibet. Most terms begin at the end of next week.
It's understood Meghan will concentrate on settling her children into the routine of life in a British school. She is not expected to embark on any kind of full programme of public engagements.
Exploring acting opportunities and running her business, As Ever, will fill her time once her family is settled. She may also appear alongside her husband at some of his charity events.
![Meghan Markle, dressed in black, smiles as she stands in front of a promotional red carpet board for the US show Suits.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/704/cpsprodpb/00ff/live/4b29b790-9fdd-11f1-9c90-a93a719154c7.jpg)
Meghan previously starred in Suits. She is seen here at the season five premiere in 2016
The couple will keep their multi-million dollar home in Montecito, about a two-hour drive north of Los Angeles. Meghan's mother, Doria Ragland, who has been heavily involved in helping to care for her grandchildren, will remain living in California.
The family is expected to return to the US regularly as well as use the holiday home they have bought near Melides in Portugal.
It is close to a property bought by Princess Eugenie and her husband Jack Brooksbank who have remained close to the Sussexes during the royal fallout.
How involved Harry, Meghan, Archie and Lilibet will be with the wider royal family has not yet been decided.
Over the next few months, several significant royal engagements are in the diary that would involve most senior royals - Remembrance Sunday at the Cenotaph, the Princess of Wales' Carol Service at Westminster Abbey and then Christmas at Sandringham.
Will there be invitations extended to the Sussex family?
Trust remains an issue. There is caution, a degree of wariness and even hostility in some quarters of the Royal Household. These decisions are very much a work in progress.
Harry and Meghan's team has described the move to the UK as being for "an extended period of time".
It is not necessarily a long-term move but may be a chance for the family to experience life in the UK, allowing the children to get to know their grandfather, the King, while they are young enough to not have their education disrupted.
Much of what happens in the months ahead will be a test - of Harry and Meghan's liking for life in the UK, of public reaction to them and of the royal family's ability to continue with their duties alongside the distractions the Sussex family may bring.
Additional reporting by James Govan.
summary: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex and their two children are preparing to relocate from California to the UK for an extended period, with plans to base themselves in the Cotswolds. Meghan is exploring a return to acting and focusing on settling their children into a British school, while Prince Harry plans to concentrate on his charity work and patronages. Meanwhile, the family's level of involvement with the wider royal family remains uncertain as trust continues to be a work in progress.
key_points: Harry, Meghan, and their two children, Archie and Lilibet, are moving from California to become residents of the UK.
Meghan is considering a return to acting and has faced speculation about a potential role in Netflix's The Gentlemen.
Prince Harry has completed his final US charity engagements and will focus on UK patronages, including the WellChild Awards and the Invictus Games.
The family is expected to base themselves in the Cotswolds and enroll their children in a British school.
Decisions regarding the Sussex family's involvement with the wider royal family remain undecided as trust is still an issue.

title: Celebrities call for protection of child actors after Hayden Panettiere’s death
author: David Mouriquand
content:
Hollywood continues to mourn the death of actress Hayden Panettiere, which has sparked discussions regarding the way the film industry treats child stars. "It’s not a coincidence that so many former, specifically pre-sexualized female, child ‘stars’ have profoundly sad lives and untimely ends."
The untimely death of actress Hayden Panettiere has renewed conversations about the lack of protections offered to child stars in the film and TV industry.
Several celebrities have spoken out regarding the protection of child actors, including Rose McGowan, Anna Paquin and Melissa Gilbert, who are all calling for tighter regulations.
McGowan and Paquin shared tributes to Panettiere, the Heroes, Nashville and Scream star who died at age 36 on 16 August, with each commenting on the “profoundly sad” treatment of child actors.
“Rest in Power Hayden Panettiere. Don’t put kids in show business,” McGowan – who appeared in the Scream franchise, wrote on social media. “None of this is normal. May her spirit be free of those who orchestrated.”
Paquin, who won an Oscar at the age of 11 for her performance in The Piano and, coincidentally, also appeared in the Scream films, echoed that sentiment, writing: “It’s not a coincidence that so many former, specifically pre-sexualized female, child ‘stars’ have profoundly sad lives and untimely ends,” she wrote on Instagram. “We were not as protected by the ‘systems’ that look great on paper, as we are supposed to be.”
She continued: “RIP [Hayden Panettiere], [Michelle Trachtenberg], [Daveigh Chase] and too many others. It’s a strange small club we belong to and you are worthy of support no matter how our industry made us feel. Literally DM me. I believe you and I will stand by your side. You aren’t alone. Let’s have each other’s backs. It might make public disclosure less terrifying.”
Michelle Trachtenberg died aged 39 in February 2025, while Daveigh Chase died in July aged 35.
Paquin later clarified that she was speaking “very specifically about the experience as a child on set that finds themselves prematurely a ‘sex object’.”
She added: “I’m not implying damage is not done outside of the context of entertainment. But that is a longer post for a different moment. Also I used the women’s initials because I ran out of space. Nothing to be read into. Just logistics.”
Melissa Gilbert shared a post on Substack over the weekend, in which she asked: “How is it possible that no one in the mainstream media has picked up on this? Within one year, Michelle Trachtenberg, Daveigh Chase and Hayden Panettiere have died. DIED! Three former female child actors of the same generation are gone. Tragically, heartbreakingly, agonizingly too soon.”
“I did not know Hayden personally and only worked briefly with Mishy and Daveigh. It feels personal because I was them,” Gilbert wrote. “We are all members of the same tribe; Female Former Child Performers, and when one of us dies, it runs through all of us like an electrical current. When three of us die so close together, something is very, very wrong. We all know the stories of how the entertainment industry uses, abuses, exploits and then throws away it’s youngest, but for some reason, this trend is getting worse.”
She later added, “Where is our Union in all of this? Where is the collective outrage? Where are the regulations? Where is the protection of privacy?”
“It really seems like no one cares enough to enact real change. At least, not until the next death and everyone talks about how sad they are and how we must do something and then they forget and get on with their lives until it happens again and again and again,” Gilbert continued. “Yes, addiction is a real disease. Family dysfunction is real. PTSD is real. In actors, all those things are assets. They enable us to access emotion and share it with an audience. But when it comes through children, it should be treated tenderly, protectively, respectfully and in a way that is as limited as possible.”
Panettiere started working in Hollywood at a young age, appearing in the soap opera One Life to Live at just four years old before starring in 2000’s Remember the Titans at 10, among other projects.
Best known for her roles in the shows Heroes and Nashville, as well as the Scream films, Panettiere was found unresponsive in Greenville, South Carolina. A 911 dispatch audio referred to a suspected “overdose”. She was pronounced dead by first responders after they administered “advanced cardiac life support.”
An official cause of death has not been disclosed and an investigation into her death is ongoing.
Read more
![Ukraine's Wladimir Klitschko and his wife Hayden Panettiere, leave the hall after Klitschko lost to Britain's Tyson Fury in a world heavyweight title fight on 29 Nov 2015.](https://images.euronews.com/articles/stories/09/87/84/62/480x270_cmsv2_cc676c28-de98-5e72-9f2c-19960de34c07-9878462.jpg) 
![Stars pay tribute to Heroes and Scream star Hayden Panettiere, dead aged 36](https://images.euronews.com/articles/stories/09/87/67/47/480x270_cmsv2_c0833c49-bfac-54c4-8c50-ea2a2c3df8da-9876747.jpg) 
![Hayden Panettiere at the 2013 Golden Globes](https://images.euronews.com/articles/stories/09/87/65/79/480x270_cmsv2_20e00f0c-83b6-586e-85e6-2ba7ff237dda-9876579.jpg)
summary: The death of actress Hayden Panettiere at age 36 has renewed industry discussions regarding the lack of protections and regulations for child stars. Several former child actors, including Rose McGowan, Anna Paquin, and Melissa Gilbert, have spoken out about the exploitation and tragic ends faced by many young performers. Gilbert and Paquin specifically questioned the role of unions and systems in failing to protect vulnerable child actors from premature sexualization and abuse.
key_points: Actress Hayden Panettiere died at age 36 in Greenville, South Carolina, with an ongoing investigation into her death.
Celebrities such as Rose McGowan, Anna Paquin, and Melissa Gilbert are calling for tighter industry regulations and better protection for child actors.
Paquin and Gilbert highlighted the recent deaths of multiple former female child actors from the same generation.
Gilbert questioned where unions, collective outrage, and privacy protections are for children working in the entertainment industry.

title: Kit Harington Joins ‘Harry Potter’ Season 2 as Gilderoy Lockhart, Replacing Nicholas Hoult
author: Ellise Shafer
content:
Kit Harington will now play Gilderoy Lockhart in Season 2 of HBO‘s “Harry Potter” series, replacing Nicholas Hoult, who exited the production due to scheduling conflicts.
The “Game of Thrones” star recently voiced Lockhart, who is central to the plot of second book “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets,” in Audible’s “Harry Potter” audiobooks late last year. Lockhart, a famous yet arrogant wizard known for his many heroic acts, becomes the new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher at Hogwarts — and it’s soon made clear that he isn’t qualified for the job. He was portrayed by Kenneth Branagh in the 2002 “Chamber of Secrets” film.
Speaking to Variety about the audiobooks in December, self-proclaimed “Harry Potter” nerd Harington said he fell in love with J.K. Rowling’s books as a kid and has reread them many times since.
Popular on Variety
“It was a really simple yes, because I love the character,” Harington said of agreeing to voice Lockhart in the audiobooks. “As far as cameos in a series go, you don’t get much more entertaining and fun to do as an actor than Gilderoy Lockhart. It was a no-brainer.”
Season 2 of the “Harry Potter” series, which is based on “Chamber of Secrets,” is set to start shooting this fall. The first season will premiere on HBO and HBO Max Christmas Day.
Dominic McLaughlin is set to play the title role in the show, with Arabella Stanton and Alastair Stout playing Hermione Granger and Ron Weasley. Additional cast members include John Lithgow as Hogwarts headmaster Dumbledore while Janet McTeer is Professor McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu plays Snape and Nick Frost has been cast as Rubeus Hagrid.
Jon Brown, a writer on the first season of the adaptation, has been promoted to serve as co-showrunner on Season 2. He joins current showrunner and series developer Francesca Gardiner. Gardiner serves as executive producer alongside director Mark Mylod. “Harry Potter” author Rowling also executive produces along with Neil Blair and Ruth Kenley-Letts of Brontë Film and TV and David Heyman of Heyday Films. Warner Bros. Television is the studio.
summary: Kit Harington has been cast as Gilderoy Lockhart for the second season of HBO's "Harry Potter" series, replacing Nicholas Hoult due to scheduling conflicts. Harington previously voiced the character in recent Audible audiobooks. Season 2, based on "Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets," is scheduled to begin filming this fall.
key_points: Kit Harington replaces Nicholas Hoult as Gilderoy Lockhart for Season 2 of HBO's "Harry Potter" series.
Harington previously voiced Lockhart in Audible's "Harry Potter" audiobooks.
Season 2 is based on the book "Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets" and begins filming this fall.
Jon Brown has been promoted to co-showrunner for Season 2 alongside Francesca Gardiner.

title: All Points East: EsDeeKid mystery no problem for rapper's fans
author: Srosh Khan; Naomi de Souza
content:
![EsDeeKid performs in front of a blow-up castle during a set in Illinois.  He is seen looking at the crowds while holding a microphone and wearing a black mask with holes and a hoodie.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/8343/live/15545740-9fb2-11f1-bff6-57f1422ebb0b.jpg)
EsDeeKid performed his first gig in the UK for a while at All Points East
- Published
There might be fewer people guessing who he is these days - but if EsDeeKid's only UK festival appearance this summer is anything to go by, no-one seems to care.
The masked rapper took to the All Points East stage on Sunday night, reeling off his signature raw and punchy bars from on top of a castle.
When EsDeeKid, who raps with a Scouse accent and only ever reveals his eyes, burst on to the scene last year everyone was convinced he was TimothÃ©e Chalamet.
But the US actor finally shot those rumours down in December by performing alongside him in a new video.
Since then the noise, rumours and conspiracy theories have died down, but it hasn't slowed his rise.
The rapper recently announced a 48-date tour, dubbed Council House Rat, featuring shows in Europe, the US and the UK.
BBC Newsbeat joined fans at All Points East to find out how one of the fastest-rising names in the UK underground rap scene is still managing to pull huge crowds - despite no-one knowing who he is.
![TimothÃ©e Chalamet wears a butter yellow suit with a gold pin on the collar.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/e176/live/02925140-9fb0-11f1-bff6-57f1422ebb0b.jpg)
TimothÃ©e Chalamet's collab with EsDeeKid went viral, with British rapper Central Cee replying "Naaa"
Festivalgoers who saw EsDeeKid's set in east London described it as "absolutely insane" with "constant energy".
"We've had proof it's not TimothÃ©e Chalamet, I think he's just some guy from Liverpool and if he is, that's exactly what I rate," fan Isaac said.
EsDeeKid's video with Oscar-nominated Chalamet racked up 42 million views on TikTok - as well as dispelling the main theory about the rapper's identity.
But Isaac hopes he isn't already famous and is instead "just some guy from Liverpool".
"I feel like the industry really needs someone who [doesn't] really have any presence in the scene," he says.
"It's really good if it's someone who is completely anonymous, I think that would be a great thing for the underground."
'He's just him, take it or leave it'
EsDeeKid dropped his debut album Rebel in June 2025 but it took a few months to cut through into the mainstream - first appearing at number 82 in the UK Official Albums Charts.
It's since gone on to reach number eight, while also peaking at 23 on the Billboard 200 chart in the US.
By the end of last year, EsDeeKid's monthly listens on Spotify had "skyrocketed", external, which Dazed said had "half of Europe rapping in his distinctive scouse accent".
Danil Boparai, a content strategy director at Dazed, thinks "the hype is justified".
"He brings a very raw energy which you see with his reluctance to do much press, no-one knows much about him, it's all about the music for him," he says.
"EsDeeKid has become one of the voices of Gen Z musically, through a unique take on rap due to his Scouse accent and his aesthetic taps into quite medieval-style fashion.
"He had a castle style set [on Sunday] which was quite unique, I haven't see that at All Points East or Outbreak festival before."
It helps that every song on the musician's debut mixtape "became like a TikTok anthem", Boparai says.
![All Points East festival goers Bin and Zari smile at the camera wearing their festival gear. Bin wears a sheer black top and has green and blonde hair with a black furry headband. Zari wears a black slogan t-shirt and has pink and green hair.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/78f0/live/64c1d0c0-9fb0-11f1-95c3-f94999de983a.jpg)
Guess who?! Fans Bin (left) and Zari say the mystery around the rapper is what makes him interesting
And his appeal has since spread across the pond.
EsDeeKid's tour will begin in North America in September, before ending in December with two hometown shows in Liverpool.
For fan James, the anonymity element is "amazing".
"I work in event promotion, I think giving yourself an aesthetic, something to cling to, something that people can watch is really important in the music industry, it makes you stand out," he says.
Decked out in a bright outfit to see EsDeeKid, fan Zari says the rapper's presence is "very mysterious".
"But that's the good thing about him, it's what brings people towards him, we're all curious."
And for Boparai, the Chalamet rumours may have been big for his brand, but having the music to back it up is crucial.
"EsDeeKid understands the internet," he says.
"It is so important to come across as truly authentic and I think he does because he lets his music do the speaking for him.
"He also doesn't change his accent, he doesn't reveal his face.
"He's just him, take it or leave it."
![A footer logo for BBC Newsbeat. It has the BBC logo and the word Newsbeat in white over a colorful background of violet, purple and orange shapes. At the bottom a black square reading "Listen on Sounds" is visible.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/0d6f/live/397f39f0-d40c-11ef-9fd6-0be88a764111.jpg)
summary: The masked and anonymous British rapper EsDeeKid drew large crowds and positive reactions during his UK festival appearance at All Points East. Although earlier rumors falsely suggested he was actor Timothée Chalamet, the speculation has not slowed the artist's rising popularity. EsDeeKid recently released his debut album, built a large social media following, and announced a 48-date international tour.
key_points: EsDeeKid performed his first UK festival appearance in a while at All Points East.
Early rumors claiming the masked rapper was Timothée Chalamet were dispelled when the actor appeared in a video with him in December.
His debut album Rebel reached number eight on the UK charts and number 23 on the US Billboard 200 chart.
EsDeeKid announced a 48-date tour titled Council House Rat, spanning Europe, the US, and the UK.

title: A new Oasis reunion? Liam Gallagher tells Noel ‘announce the tour’
author: Roisin O'Connor
content:
“Ffs RKID announce the tour we’re all losing our minds.” So said the latest tantalising post from the world’s biggest wind-up merchant Liam Gallagher. Fans might stay sceptical... but could this in fact be the clearest indicator yet that another Oasis reunion is on the cards?
By now, a new tour might seem less of a surprise than those long-awaited 2025 shows. The rock band made history when brothers Noel and Liam Gallagher put an end to their years-long feud and reunited onstage for the first time in almost 16 years to play a record-breaking world tour, including a series of homecoming shows in Manchester.
Even before the 2025 tour concluded, fans predicted that Oasis would be keen to get back out on the road again, given the run of shows were a defining cultural event – as well as a very lucrative one. Oasis Live ‘25 was estimated by Forbes to have generated over $400m (£293m) in revenue, with Noel and Liam each pocketing between $50m-$100m. As a result, the pair cracked the Sunday Times Rich List this year with a combined net worth of $375m.
The Independent’s sources have said they understand that a Knebworth residency is on the cards but have yet to confirm any specific dates. This year marked the 30th anniversary of the band’s legendary Knebworth shows in 1996, where they played to a combined audience of 250,000 (more than four per cent of the population applied for tickets), including the rumoured 7,000-strong guestlist.
![Oasis at Knebworth, August 1996](https://static.the-independent.com/2025/06/25/09/13112940-4ca3860b-788d-4a10-99d9-8e7270096092.jpg)
Sources have also said that Noel has been writing new music – it remains to be seen if this will emerge in the shape of the first Oasis album since 2008’s Dig Out Your Soul, with Liam on vocal duties.
Earlier this month, it was announced that SJM Concerts, the promoter behind the Oasis reunion tour, had secured a licence to host events at Knebworth indefinitely.
The promoter has also worked on shows with Take That and The Prodigy, as well as comedian Peter Kay.
The licence allows events for up to 125,000 people, with live music and dance performances permitted until 3am.
In July, The Sun claimed that Oasis would play six nights at Knebworth over a three-week period in September 2027. Meanwhile, the Manchester Evening News reported that same month that the rock’n’roll stars would headline 12 nights at the Etihad stadium, with an insider telling the paper: “It will be 12 nights at the Etihad Stadium across May and June. They could even add more dates to that as well, there’s talk of up to 20. The wider tour is also going to include a return to Knebworth.”
Before that, there was speculation in 2024 – after the band announced their comeback tour – that they would return to the site. Oasis denied this on X in a statement: “Contrary to reports in some UK tabloid media today, Oasis will not be playing Knebworth Park in the future.”
The Independent has contacted Oasis’s representatives for comment.
![Brothers Liam and Noel Gallagher during their 2025 reunion tour](https://static.the-independent.com/2025/09/24/9/00/SEI263754364.jpeg)
Contrary to tabloid media reports, sources told The Independent that the mood backstage during Oasis’s 2025 reunion was jubilant, with both Noel and Liam in great spirits as their famous friends – from football stars to pop singers, including Manchester City star Jack Grealish and the Happy Mondays’ Shaun Ryder – rubbed elbows.
“It’s been a proper love-in backstage,” one source said. “There’s a friends and family bar which is basically free booze – Guinness on draft (of course) (sic), beer, wine and champagne. It’s like going to a wedding every night.”
They continued: “Cast and Richard Ashcroft [Oasis’s support acts] are having the time of their lives – it’s been so nice to see Noel and Liam’s guests vibing off each other. Everyone’s been making new friends.”
And while it was true that Liam had left early each night – this was nothing to do with animosity towards his older brother and everything to do with him ensuring he was in peak condition for each concert.
“Liam has been completely zen, focusing on his voice and arriving shortly before each show, then getting straight off to avoid temptation,” a source told The Independent.
The 2025 reunion tour is the subject of a forthcoming documentary directed by Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight, due for release in IMAX cinemas on 9 September and on Disney+. Titled Don’t Look Back In Anger, the film follows Noel and Liam as they undertake the Live ‘25 tour, which kicked off just over a year ago in Cardiff.
A 46-second teaser trailer, released last month, showed cheering fans before cutting to footage of the Gallagher siblings backstage getting ready for their first shows together since their split in 2009.
“Oasis Live ‘25, one of the most anticipated rock ‘n’ roll comebacks of our time,” Disney+ said in a statement. “The film is an unapologetically uplifting account of the biggest musical event of 2025, capturing the experience and emotions of the band and their fans across the world.
“The unique perspective includes rehearsal, backstage, and onstage access as well as the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in over 20 years.”
When it comes to Glastonbury, Liam insisted over the weekend that an Oasis headline performance is “not happening” next year. Organiser Emily Eavis recently confirmed that all headliners have been booked.
As for a 2027 tour, for now, Oasis fans will just have to roll with it... the band are taking their time.
summary: Following their successful and lucrative 2025 reunion tour, Liam Gallagher has posted a hint on social media urging Noel to announce a new tour. Sources indicate that a Knebworth residency and multiple stadium shows are being discussed, and that Noel has been writing new music. Additionally, a documentary about the 2025 reunion, titled Don't Look Back In Anger, is set for release in September on Disney+ and in IMAX.
key_points: Liam Gallagher posted a message on social media prompting Noel to announce a new Oasis tour.
The 2025 reunion tour generated over $400m in revenue and placed the brothers on the Sunday Times Rich List.
Sources suggest a Knebworth residency and up to 20 nights at the Etihad Stadium could be part of future plans.
A documentary titled Don't Look Back In Anger, directed by Steven Knight, will be released on Disney+ and in IMAX cinemas.
Liam Gallagher stated that an Oasis headline performance at Glastonbury next year is not happening.

title: ‘The Gentlemen’ Officially Renewed for Season 3 as First Season 2 Trailer Drops: ‘I’m Looking Forward to Pushing the Boundaries Further,’ Guy Ritchie Says (EXCLUSIVE)
author: K J Yossman
content:
“The Gentlemen” has officially been greenlit for Season 3, Variety can confirm.
Guy Ritchie’s high-society, high-octane caper starring Theo James and Kaya Scodelario is set to return for a third outing, comprised of eight episodes. Variety understands that while the new season is in pre-production no scripts have yet been finalized, let alone new casting, despite rumors of Meghan Markle joining. The show is due to go into production imminently.
“The ambition of ‘The Gentlemen’ has accelerated, the world has expanded and the consequences carry weight,” says creator, writer, director and executive producer Guy Ritchie. “A third season felt inevitable, and I’m looking forward to pushing the boundaries of it further.”
Popular on Variety
Ritchie will also be returning to direct Season 3, which he co-writes with Matthew Read.
The news of the third season comes amid a host of returning season orders for some of Netflix’s top U.K. shows including “Black Mirror” Season 8, “Legends” Season 2 and “Being Gordon Ramsay” Season 2. Other highly anticipated Netflix U.K. dramas returning for a second season are “Supacell,” “Black Doves” and “House of Guinness.”
The streamer today also released its first full-length trailer for “The Gentlemen” Season 2, ahead of its launch on Sept. 3.
![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
Season 2 will see Eddie Horniman (James) and Susie Glass (Scodelario) grow their business internationally as they take to the lakeside villas of Italy where at least one of their crew finds out he’s bitten off more than he can chew.
Meanwhile Eddie’s rise through the criminal underworld is mirrored by his rise through the British establishment, bringing him into the circle of a new oleaginous aristo played by Hugh Bonneville, who is joining the cast.
In the trailer, Eddie hints at his growing ambitions, as he tells Geoff of his stately pile: “Four hundred years ago, this estate spread out as far as the eye could see. I want it all back.”
With American billionaire Stanley Johnston (Giancarlo Esposito) whispering in his hear (“You are destined to rule, forge your own path”) Eddie’s confidence in his ability to play high-stakes games with notorious crime lords soars ever higher — but at what cost?
Season 2 sees Ray Winstone returning as Glass’s kingpin father Bobby while Harry Goodwins returns as her brawny brother Jack.
On the Duke’s side, Joely Richardson is back as Eddie’s mother Lady Sabrina, Daniel Ings as disinherited older brother Freddy, Jasmine Blackborow as sister Charly and Vinnie Jones as Geoff, keeper of the grounds – and family secrets.
![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
Also returning for Season 2 are Esposito, Michael Vu, Ruby Sear and Pearce Quigley.
Joining the cast this season are Benjamin Clementine (“Dune”), Benedetta Porcaroli (“The Leopard”), Amra Mallassi (“Dune: Part Two”), Tyler Conti (“Tell Me Everything”), professional boxer Chris Eubank Jr and “Love Island U.K.” host Maya Jama.
“The Gentlemen” is produced by Moonage Pictures for Netflix and Miramax TV. Exec producers are Ritchie, Read, Ivan Atkinson, Will Gould, Simon Crawford, Collins and Frith Tiplady for Moonage Pictures alongside Jonathan Glickman and Marc Helwig for Miramax TV,
Check out the new trailer below:
summary: Netflix has officially renewed Guy Ritchie's series "The Gentlemen" for an eight-episode third season ahead of its season two premiere. Season two, set to launch on September 3, features expanding international operations and new cast members including Hugh Bonneville. Meanwhile, season three is currently in pre-production with no final scripts or casting decisions yet made.
key_points: "The Gentlemen" has been officially greenlit for an eight-episode Season 3.
Season 3 is currently in pre-production with no scripts finalized or new casting confirmed.
Netflix released the first full-length trailer for Season 2, which premieres on September 3.
Season 2 features returning cast members alongside new additions such as Hugh Bonneville.

title: Meghan Markle is reportedly dropped from Netflix series after ‘intense’ backlash
author: Carsen Holaday
content:
Meghan Markle may not be appearing in the third season of Guy Ritchie’s The Gentlemen after all.
This week, reports that the Duchess of Sussex, 45, was considering a return to acting in the Netflix series sparked waves of backlash in the U.K.
Now, former Vanity Fair and New York Magazine editor-in-chief Tina Brown claims the decision to cast Meghan in the drama has been reversed.
“I learned this morning that the casting of Meghan Markle in season 3 of Guy Ritchie’s Netflix series The Gentlemen has been withdrawn,” Brown — who is the author of two books about the Royal Family — wrote on her Substack Saturday.
“The backlash in the UK was so intense, it became untenable to go forward,” she added.
The Independent has reached out to Netflix, Meghan and Ritchie for comment.
According to Variety, Meghan was in discussions to join the third installment of the series, starring Theo James and Kaya Scodelario, which films in the U.K.
The show is a spin-off of Guy Ritchie’s popular 2019 crime comedy movie of the same name, which starred Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam and Colin Farrell.
The third season of the show has not been officially greenlit. Season two premieres September 3.
The duke and duchess revealed earlier this month that they would be moving from California back to the U.K. with their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, who are both enrolled in British schools, six years after they came to the U.S.
![Guy Ritchie’s ‘The Gentlemen’ films in the UK, where Harry and Meghan are returning after six years in the US](https://static.the-independent.com/2023/11/30/12/TG_101_Unit_01121_COMP_NEW_RT.jpg)
Brown reported that the upcoming move across the pond was partly inspired by Meghan’s potential gig in The Gentlemen.
It would have been her first acting role since she quit performing in 2017, when she got engaged to Prince Harry.
However, she recently appeared on screen in a cameo as herself in the upcoming Amazon MGM comedy Close Personal Friends, which stars Lily Collins and Brie Larson.
It marked Meghan’s first performance in nearly a decade after she rose to fame for her role as Rachel Zane in seven seasons of the legal drama Suits. She also appeared in films including Horrible Bosses, A Lot Like Love and Random Encounters.
Powerful leaders in the entertainment industry have spoken out to say that directors and producers will undoubtedly be eager to meet with Meghan if she has officially decided to resume her acting career.
summary: Reports indicate that Meghan Markle's potential casting in the third season of Netflix's 'The Gentlemen' has been withdrawn following intense backlash in the U.K. According to former magazine editor Tina Brown, the negative reaction made moving forward with the role untenable. The third season of the series has not yet been officially greenlit.
key_points: Meghan Markle was reportedly considered for a role in season three of Guy Ritchie's Netflix series The Gentlemen.
Tina Brown stated that the casting decision was reversed due to intense backlash in the U.K.
The third season of the show has not yet received an official greenlight.
Meghan previously quit acting in 2017 upon her engagement to Prince Harry after starring in the legal drama Suits.

title: Race Across the World star Jo Gardiner dies a year after son
author: Kevin Rawlinson
content:
Tributes have been paid to the Race Across the World star Jo Gardiner, who has died a year after her son and co-star Sam was killed in a car crash.
The physiotherapist from Manchester died after “a long and courageous battle with cancer”, relatives said. She was 61 and is survived by her other son, Charlie.
She and Sam competed in the second series of the BBC’s global travel competition, journeying across South America together in 2020.
Relatives remembered her as “an intrepid adventurer” who was “brave, kind, witty and endlessly loving”.
Her family said: “She had a rare gift for making everyone around her feel more alive. She lived fully, fiercely and never did anything by halves. She was blessed with countless friends, drawn to her extraordinary magnetism. Somehow, each one felt as though they were among her very best.
“To us, she was more than all of these things. She was our family, our joy, our safe place and our absolute treasure. We know how deeply Jo was loved, and we take comfort in knowing that her laughter, her courage, her kindness and her wonderfully outrageous spirit will live on in the many people whose lives she touched.”
![Jo Gardiner in a PR image for Race Across the World](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/2820b6382c2157febd5aaace20a6ccebcc1e0202/1131_196_2982_2386/master/2982.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The family asked that those who knew and loved her “do exactly what she would have wanted: tell the funny stories, raise a glass, have an adventure, laugh loudly and live life to the full.”
They added: “She was one of a kind. There will never be another her.”
Sam Gardiner died in June 2025 at the age of 24 after his car came off the road, rolled and landed on its side.
The mother and son competed on Race Across the World because Jo wanted to have a travel adventure with Sam, who had ADHD. They competed against four other pairs of contestants racing from Mexico City down to Ushuaia in Argentina.
A spokesperson for the programme said: “On behalf of the Studio Lambert production team, the BBC and the whole Race Across the World cast, we offer our deepest and heartfelt sympathies to Jo’s son Charlie and her wider family and friends.
“Millions of people remembered their transformative journey across Latin America in 2020 and we hold that memory in our hearts as we fondly recall Jo’s passion for life, her kindness, her strength and above all her utter devotion to Sam and her family.”
Jo Gardiner had type 1 diabetes and was an ambassador for Diabetes UK. Her family has set up a JustGiving page in her name and said all donations are to support the charity.
summary: Jo Gardiner, a physiotherapist and star of the BBC show Race Across the World, has died at the age of 61 following a long battle with cancer. Her death comes a year after her son and co-star Sam was killed in a car crash. Gardiner is survived by her other son, Charlie, and was remembered by her family and the show's producers for her adventurous spirit, kindness, and devotion.
key_points: Jo Gardiner passed away at 61 after a long battle with cancer.
She and her son Sam previously competed in the second series of Race Across the World in 2020.
Sam Gardiner had died a year prior in a car crash at the age of 24.
Gardiner was a type 1 diabetes ambassador, and her family set up a JustGiving page to support Diabetes UK in her honor.

title: Jo Gardiner Dead: 'Race Across The World' Star Passes A Year After Son
author: Jake Kanter
content:
![Jo and Sam Gardiner](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/EastI-Standard-image-2026-08-24T104343.967.jpg?w=681&h=383&crop=1) 
Jo Gardiner, star of the second season of Race Across the World, has died. She was 61.
Gardiner’s family said she died after a “long and courageous battle with cancer.” Her passing comes a year after her son, Sam, lost his life in a car crash in 2025.
Jo and Sam competed together in Race Across the World, traversing Latin America for the BBC reality competition series, produced by Studio Lambert. They became firm favorites among fans of the show, finishing fourth in their race.
“She lived fully, fiercely and never did anything by halves,” Jo’s family said in a statement, shared with BBC News.
“She was blessed with countless friends, drawn to her extraordinary magnetism. Somehow, each one felt as though they were among her very best. To us, she was more than all of these things. She was our family, our joy, our safe place and our absolute treasure.”
Watch on Deadline
In a statement, Studio Lambert and the BBC said: “We offer our deepest and heartfelt sympathies to Jo’s son Charlie, and her wider family and friends.
“Following the tragic death of Jo’s son Sam last year, we paid tribute to how integral Sam and Jo had been to series two. Millions of people remembered their transformative journey across Latin America in 2020 and we hold that memory in our hearts as we fondly recall Jo’s passion for life, her kindness, her strength, and above all her utter devotion to Sam and her family.
“At the time of filming, Sam described his mum as amazing – and that is how we will always remember her. Jo became the matriarch of the Race Across the World cast family, she leaves a lasting legacy in the many lives that she touched, both through the series and beyond. It was a privilege to share her story and she will be deeply missed.”
summary: Jo Gardiner, a star of the reality television series "Race Across The World," has died at the age of 61 following a battle with cancer. Her passing occurs one year after the death of her son, Sam, with whom she competed on the second season of the BBC show. Family, the BBC, and production company Studio Lambert paid tribute to her memory, strength, and legacy.
key_points: Jo Gardiner passed away at age 61 after a battle with cancer.
She competed alongside her son Sam on season two of "Race Across The World," finishing fourth.
Her death comes one year after her son Sam died in a car crash in 2025.
The BBC and Studio Lambert released a statement honoring her kindness, strength, and devotion to her family.

title: Dutch broadcaster Avrotros pulls out of 2027 Eurovision Song Contest
author: Paul Glynn
content:
![Spectators wearing raincoats in rainbow colours gather at the fan area in front of the City Hall in Vienna on May 14, 2026, prior to the second semi-final of the Eurovision Song Contest (ESC).](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/c11e/live/6c8b6380-9fb4-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
- Published
Dutch public broadcaster Avrotros has pulled out of next year's Eurovision Song Contest, saying that the competition can no longer be considered neutral while a participating country remains involved in a large-scale military conflict.
In a statement, external released on Monday, the broadcaster said the decision was due to a lack of clarity from organisers - the Eurovision Broadcasting Union (EBU) - over assessing which countries could compete.
Avrotros added: "The severe humanitarian suffering in Gaza and the ongoing restrictions on press freedom have contributed to increasing divisions surrounding the Eurovision Song Contest in recent years."
Earlier this month, the EBU updated their rules to state that if a country involved in an armed conflict wins the competition, it will be ineligible to host it the following year. But Avrotros said those changes "do not provide sufficient confidence that âthe â independent and neutral character of the Eurovision Song Contest has been restored."
The broadcaster's withdrawal from this year's contest in Burgas, Bulgaria, does not necessarily rule out Dutch participation in Eurovision 2027.
Another broadcaster within the Dutch public broadcasting system could potentially take it on as the country has several public broadcasters, unlike the UK.
But the Netherlands boycotted this year's contest in Vienna, Austria, after Israel were allowed to compete.
Only Ireland and Sweden have won Eurovision more than the Netherlands.
Martin Green, director of the contest, said in a statement that the EBU regretted Avrotros's decision but respected its views.
"We will now continue our dialogue with NPO, the umbrella organization for Dutch public service media, regarding the opportunities for another broadcaster to participate. We very much hope that audiences and artists in the Netherlands can continue to be represented in the Eurovision Song Contest."
'Platform for division'
Taco Zimmerman, director general of Avrotos, said the Eurovision Song Contest "was originally created to bring people and countries together" but was now "a platform for division".
He said: "It is undeniable that international conflicts are increasingly affecting the contest, undermining its neutral character.
"The Eurovision Song Contest has therefore become a platform for division. As a public broadcaster, we remain committed to our values."
He added: "They guide us in everything we do, even when that means stepping away from an event that is very close to our hearts. That is painful as we would have very much liked to be part of the contest again next year."
Green, however, stated that the contest "has always been a place to bring people together, celebrate diverse communities, and show that a better world is possible even in the most difficult times."
New rules
The recent amendment to the rules, that mean a country involved in an armed military conflict can't host the next contest if it wins, was approved by the contest's governing body, following feedback from participating broadcasters after Eurovision 2026.
It stated that winning countries will also be disqualified from hosting if a "sensitive geopolitical situation" affects the "security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region".
Last November, following a failed attempt to have Israel suspended, five broadcasters announced they were boycotting the competition - including Eurovision powerhouses Spain, Ireland and the Netherlands.
Despite the protests, Israel's Noam Bettan ultimately took second place with his song Michelle.
It marked the second year in a row that Israel had taken the runners-up position - and some participating broadcasters have privately expressed safety concerns over the contest being staged in Jerusalem or Tel Aviv, should the country win in the future.
Although Israel will undoubtedly be seen as the target of the rule change, it will also affect Ukraine, which has been engaged in a protracted war since it was invaded by Russia in 2022.
Ukrainian group Kalush Orchestra went on to win Eurovision that same year, in a symbolic show of public support.
summary: Dutch public broadcaster Avrotros has withdrawn from the Eurovision Song Contest due to concerns that the event has lost its neutrality amid ongoing military conflicts. The decision follows a lack of clarity from organizers, the European Broadcasting Union (EBU), regarding participation rules. Despite Avrotros's exit, another Dutch public broadcaster could potentially participate in the future.
key_points: Dutch broadcaster Avrotros pulled out of the Eurovision Song Contest citing a loss of neutrality over a participating country's involvement in a military conflict.
The EBU recently updated rules stating a winning country involved in an armed conflict cannot host the following year, but Avrotros deemed this insufficient.
Avrotros stated that the humanitarian suffering in Gaza and restrictions on press freedom have turned the contest into a platform for division.
Another Dutch public broadcaster could potentially take over participation, as the Netherlands has multiple public broadcasters.
The Netherlands previously boycotted the contest in Vienna after Israel was allowed to compete.

title: Hayley Atwell: Agent Carter Death "Complete Disservice" To Character
author: Jake Kanter
content:
![Hayley Atwell](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Doctor-Strange-in-the-Multiverse-of-Madness-071323-5ca38f34cdb74b6a9c6946bdc943909b-e1787556087643.jpg?w=681&h=383&crop=1) 
Hayley Atwell was disappointed about the demise of Peggy Carter.
In an interview at the For the Love of Fantasy & Sci-Fi convention in London, Atwell told attendees that she was frustrated by Captain Carter’s storyline in 2022’s Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.
Cameoing in the film as an alternate to Captain America, Carter — an MCU fixture since 2011 — was apparently killed off by Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen) with her own shield.
Atwell said: “If I’m really like brutally honest, I was so disappointed with how they positioned her and what happened to her in that scene. It’s so small, and she gets frisbeed to death.”
The actress said she pleaded with colleagues on set to make changes to the scene. “I tried on set to kind of go, ‘Can I just add? Can I just suggest?’ And they were like, ‘Sure, but no.'”

She continued: “I felt that was like a bum steer and a complete disservice to the character.”
Atwell, who is expected to return as Carter in Avengers: Doomsday later this year, said the character was having “fun” in the Captain Carter guise — and she hopes for more of the same. “I hope maybe one day in the future they’ll give her more in that capacity,” she teased.
It’s not the first time Atwell has discussed her misgivings about Carter’s cameo in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.
In 2023, she told the Happy Sad Confused podcast: “When she was like, ‘I could do this all day’ and then followed by she’s immediately cut in half by a frisbee. And the audience being like, ‘She can’t do it all day. Apparently you can’t, so, egg on your face.’ That doesn’t really serve Peggy very well.”
Earlier in the For the Love of Fantasy & Sci-Fi interview, Atwell revealed that she uses Carter’s line “I know my value” in her contract negotiations with Marvel. “If I’m able to say these lines with conviction, I’ve got to embody them myself,” she added.
summary: Actress Hayley Atwell expressed strong disappointment over Peggy Carter's brief death scene in the 2022 film Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. Atwell felt that having the character killed off quickly with her own shield was a complete disservice and a bum steer. Despite her frustrations with that cameo, Atwell is expected to return as Carter in Avengers: Doomsday.
